## Lorsque la demande d'ERAR est reçue au BRA-Vancouver

1. Recherchez le client en utilisant les fonctions Recherche-Identificateur ou Recherche-Intégrée.
Vous pouvez également rechercher le numéro de cas de Renvoi (c.-à-d. Z00000012345) à l'écran IMM.

2. Trouvez le cas de renvoi (c.-à-d. Z0000012345) sous SMGC – Antécédents de la personne, cliquez sur l’hyperlien.
3. Allez à la vue Admissibilités – Décision.
Saisir les données de la demande d'ERAR

1. Allez à la vue Admissibilités – Décision du cas de renvoi (nº commençant par Z)
## 2. Notez l’État entré par l'ASFC.

IMPORTANT: L’état de l’activité « Recevable ERAR » n’est PAS saisi dans Historique. Il est essentiel que, si le personnel chargé du triage voit que l’état est « Recevable A112(3) » lorsqu’il entre ERAR

## reçu, il garde en mémoire que cette information devra être entrée dans la demande d’ERAR.

## 3. Changez l’État de l’activité ERAR recevable pour une des valeurs.

# 4. Dans le champ Résultat au menu déroulant, sélectionnez la valeur appropriée.

## 5. Dans le champ Raison au menu déroulant, sélectionnez la valeur appropriée.

6. Enregistrez la Date de décision, qui est égale à la date à laquelle la demande a été reçue.
## 7. Sauvegardez l’information (CTRL + S).

### Aller à la demande d'ERAR

1. Au cas de renvoi (nº commençant par Z), allez à l’onglet Associations.
2. Cliquez sur l’hyperlien du champ du Nº de la demande afin d’entrer la demande d’ERAR.
Remarque : Comme le cas de renvoi (nº commençant par Z), la demande d’ERAR est créée à l’écran IMM-ÉXE.

# Entrer des observations relatives à la demande d'ERAR

1. Allez à l’onglet Correspondance dans la demande d’ERAR (nº commençant par J).
## 2. Cliquez sur le sous-onglet Reçue. 3. Cliquez sur Nouveau.

4. Cliquez sur l’applet GVM situé dans le champ IUC.
5. Mettez votre client en évidence et cliquez sur OK.
6. Allez au champ Élément et cliquez sur l’applet GVM. 7. À la fenêtre contextuelle Élément, recherchez « Observations ».
8. Cliquez sur OK.
# 9. Entrez l’information applicable pour les champs : • Via;

# Date (si elle diffère de la date que vous avez entrée dans le SMGC);

Entrez des commentaires le cas échéant (c.-à-d. observations reçues liées aux demandes d’ERAR et CH).

10. Laissez l’état à Non commencé.
11. Scannez et téléchargez les observations dans Pièces jointes le cas échéant

## Audience

Si une audience est requise pour une demande ERAR, vous devez entrer cette information au SMGC en faisant ce qui suit:

1. Naviguez jusqu’à l’onglet Événements dans la demande ERAR (J000...)
#### 2. Cliquez Nouveau 3. Entrez l’information comme ceci :

# a. Événement→ Audience

### b. But → Audience ERAR

#### c. Lieu – Heure/Date de début → entrez la date et l’heure de votre audience*

### 4. Le demandeur est automatiquement ajouté à l’événement, mais vous pouvez ajouter

manuellement une partie (représentant), en l’ajoutant dans l’applet. Pour les familles, vous devez entrer l’audience dans chaque demande.

5. Enregistrez l’information
* La durée de l’événement est fixée à 60 minutes par défaut. Vous pouvez ajuster le temps prévu en cliquant sur l’hyperlien ID Événement. Une fois l’audience terminée, ou si elle doit être reportée, mettez à jour l’information de l’onglet Événements en remplissant le champ « Résultat de l’événement » et dans l’applet, en remplissant le champ « Présent » sous le Client et si applicable, la Partie. Note : pour l’instant, il n’est pas possible d’entrer la lettre de convocation sous l’onglet Correspondance. Les présentes procédures seront ajustées lorsqu’il sera possible de le faire.
### Finaliser la décision relative à l'ERAR

1. Allez à la vue IMM – EXÉ > Admissibilités – Décision de l’ERAR (n° commençant par J).
#### 2. Faites défiler vers le bas jusqu’à l’activité Agent d’immigration principal et faites passer

## Générer la lettre de décision

# 1. Allez à la vue Correspondance – Envoyée.

## 2. Dans le champ Demande de délivrance, choisissez « Lettre ».

3. Dans le champ Genre de document, cliquez sur l’applet GVM afin de choisir le modèle.
## 4. Choisissez le modèle « Lettre de décision ».

5. Cliquez sur OK.
6. Dans le champ à menu déroulant État, faites passer l’état de Non commencé à Générer. IMPORTANT : Il est important de préciser que CIC laissera l’état de la lettre de décision à Générer.
## 7. Appuyez sur ALT + Entrée.

# 8. À l’applet Correspondance-pièces jointes, ouvrez l’hyperlien Word LTR.

9. Préparez la lettre et sauvegardez-la dans le SMGC.
10. Sauvegardez l’information (CTRL +S).
# Terminer l'ERAR/Informer l'ASFC

1. Dans la demande d’ERAR (nº commençant par J), allez à la vue Associations. Le système affiche par défaut la vue Associations – Demandes & Cas.
## 2. Cliquez sur l’hyperlien dans le champ Nº dem/cas pour le cas de renvoi.

# Le système affiche la demande de renvoi (c.-à-d. z0000012345).

3. Insérez un hyperlien dans le cas de renvoi.
4. Allez au sous-onglet Admissibilités – Décision du cas de renvoi (nº commençant par Z).
5. Faites défiler l’écran vers le bas jusqu’à l’activité « Admissible à un ERAR » et changez l’État de « ERAR reçu » à « ERAR mené à bien ».

# *** Instructions intérimaires, à être utilisées jusqu’en juin 2018. Pour plus d’information, contactez

Chaque bureau recevra mensuellement un rapport qui indiquera les demandeurs qui sont devenus RP et qui ont un ERAR dont l’état est “En attente”. L’ERAR doit être annulé pour ces clients en utilisant les

Si le demandeur n’a jamais été informé que son ERAR était fermé/en attente, faites les entrées au SNGC et envoyez la lettre au client pour confirmer que son ERAR est fermé (pas besoin de passer par l’ASFC, puisque le client est résident permanent). Vous aurez peut-être à ajuster la lettre en conséquence.

Si le client avait déjà été informé que son ERAR était fermé/en attente (comme dans les cas combo), aucune autre action n’est requise.

### Finaliser la décision relative à l'ERAR (aucun cas de renvoi dans le SMGC)

1. Allez à la vue IMM – EXÉ > Admissibilités – Décision de l’ERAR (n° commençant par J).
### 2. Faites défiler vers le bas jusqu’à l’activité Agent d’immigration principal et faites passer

l’État de Non commencé à la décision appropriée.

### 3. Dans le menu déroulant Raison, sélectionnez la valeur appropriée.

#### 4. Appuyez sur (ALT + Enter).

### Générer la lettre de décision 1. Allez à la vue Correspondance – Envoyée.

2. Dans le champ Demande de délivrance, choisissez « Lettre ».
3. Dans le champ Genre de document, cliquez sur l’applet GVM afin de choisir le modèle.
4. Choisissez le modèle « Lettre de décision ».
5. Cliquez sur OK.
6. Dans le champ à menu déroulant État, faites passer l’état de Non commencé à Générer. IMPORTANT : Il est important de préciser que CIC laissera l’état de la lettre de décision à Générer.
# 7. Appuyez sur ALT + Entrée.

#### 8. À l’applet Correspondance-pièces jointes, ouvrez l’hyperlien Word LTR.

9. Préparez la lettre et sauvegardez-la dans le SMGC.
10. Sauvegardez l’information (CTRL +S).
L'ASFC a confirmé qu'ils vont solliciter les ERAR complets en utilisant les rapports SNGC. Ils vont utiliser

#### ces rapports pour localiser les applications d’ERAR et les entrées nécessaires pour que demande d'ERAR

soit fermée.

### Subject:

Jan-20

## Hello,

Thank you for your question. At the time of issuance, this citizenship card had an expiry date due to a section of the Citizenship Act that required citizens born abroad in the second generation to retain their citizenship by their 28th birthday or be subject to loss of citizenship. However, this section of the Act has since been repealed (in 2009). The expiry date has no effect on the citizenship status of this card holder because their 28th birthday did not happen prior to the section of the Act being repealed. Therefore, the card is valid and will remain valid after the expiry date.

It is up to third parties whether to accept the citizenship card as proof of ID.

Approved by: Corrina Clement Cit ops: close

# Hello,

Follow-up-We received a question regarding a Certificate of Canadian Citizen with an expiry date along the

## side of the holder's photograph.

### Intranet-Notes

The certificates may have an expiry date when they are issued to persons who are subject to a retention of citizenship requirement. The expiry date (the holder's 28th birthday) will appear in red ink along the side of the holder's photograph. We do not accept expired Certificates of Canadian

## Citizenship as proof of identity.

To: Ghani.Fateema <Fateema.Ghani@cic.gc.ca> Cc: CN HQ PR / RP AC RC (IRCC) <IRCC.CNHQPR-RPACRC.IRCC@cic.gc.ca>; IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC) <IRCC.IPGFunctionalGuidance- OrientationFonctionnelleOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca>

## Hello Fateema,

Thank you for your patience as we had several consultations on this case.

As you mentioned, given the GCMS limitations with regard to changing the category to FCC from an FC1, we would advise that the FC1 be withdrawn an d a new FCC application is created to process under the existing appeal allowed FC1. To ensure that we are able to capture the history of the application, the officer must include all the notes from the FC1 application and to cross-reference the previous application including why an FCC is now being created (as per IAD decision). Doing so would also reflect the category under which the application is being processed and the specific category printed on the CoPR document. This would avoid further confusion if or when the client receives it.

The lAD decision for this case refers to the Tabesh conversion, which permits the conversion of a family class sponsorship based on marriage to a common-law application and referenced the case of Perry v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2011. For this specific case, the FC1 file was withdrawn and recreated as FCC.

For the integrity of data, the better approach may be to create a new FCC file and closing the FC1 file as withdrawn. This would avoid counting twice the application for the same applicant.

Additionally, the officer must continue to be satisfied that the relationship meets legal requirements, in this case of the prescribed category of common-law partner sponsorship, and is genuine. The appeal-allowed decision and prescribed switch in category should be clearly documented in GCMS notes.

We hope you find this information useful.

# Julie

# Enquiry:

From: DiCaprio.Anna Sent: January 21, 2020 11:14 AM

#### To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC) Subject NAME :/ UCl APPLICATION

##### Importance: High

## Good day,

Hope this email finds you well. I am processing this application and it is ready to be concluded however the following note states not to land...and to contact IPG. Can you kindly provide me with an update on this note

Kindest regards,

##### Anna DiCaprio CPA

, Domestic Network Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada / Government of Canada Anna.DiCaprio@cic.gc.ca/ Tel: 647-789-6576

, Réseau national Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada / Gouvernement du Canada Anna.DiCaprio@cic.gc.ca/ Tél.: 647-789-6576

### Response:

Good day Anna,

##### Thank you for your enquiry.

Program delivery instructions on excluded family members can be found in the IRCC website under the section Family class: Excluded relationships.

As per R125(1)(d), a foreign national is not a member of the family class if they were a non-accompanying family member of the sponsor and were not examined [R5, R117(9)(d), R117(10) and (11)

#### and R125(1)(d), R125(2) and (3)].

Foreign nationals sponsored under the family class may be exempt from paragraph R125 1) d) if they meet the requirements of the temporary public policy. In this case, the sponsor's spouse would have been considered a non-accompanying family member (who was not examined) at the time of the sponsor's application for permanent residence in 2014. The officer may refer to the PDIs on the "Pilot

2A-2019-16114-000034

### program to exempt permanent residence applicants in the family class from paragraph R117(9)(d) or

R125{1)(d) exclusion" for information on eligibility and admissibility requirements. Please note that the new public policy would apply in cases where the foreign national, if declared and examined at the time their sponsor immigrated to Canada, would not have made their sponsor ineligible.

If further support is required for this case specific enquiry, please contact CMB Immigration Case Advice /Conseil Cas Immigration DGRC (IRCC).

##### Trusting your concerns have been addressed.

# Enquiry:

#### Good morning IPG,

We have received the information attached concerning a modification into ENF 19. When we consult the Updates to chapter, it seems that the latest updates are not listed. We can only see 2018-08-03.

Would it be possible to include what was updated and the date, as it is currently hard to find what has

## changed? Thank you,

#### Josée Cuerrier

#### Response:

##### Thank you for your enquiry.

Please note that ENF 19 is published by CBSA, as such we have consulted with CBSA to respond to this request.

CBSA has confirmed that minor edits, as well as clarifications, have been provided throughout the chapter. Some sections were re-organized to allow for a more logical flow of information. The appendices have also been redesigned.

Also, new content has been added to reflect legislative and regulatory amendments and to ensure

### consistent application of IRPA provisions, as clarified through new court decisions. Specific updates

include:

4. Instrument of delegation and designation has been expanded to detail the appropriate Minister responsible for appeals. New section: 11.8 Permanent resident visa holders

## To: @international.gc.ca'

#### Cc: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

### Subject:RE: C10 --- IM-2020-0280 -- DUE March 17, 2020

### Good day

The IMM 5802 form is necessary for alternate submissions when an employer is unable to submit an offer of employment through the employer portal. Part of this process is for the employer to obtain the authorization of letting the employee submit the offer of employment directly with their work permit application. Once the request is approved by Immigration Program Guidance, a note is added on file to notify the processing office.

The item identified as "IMM 5802" is actually a letter indicating the LMIA exemption number, which is the same currently matched to the work permit. Therefore, this would not constitute an alternate submission and we recommend that your office continue the processing as usual.

Let me also provide you with the link on where you can find additional information on the alternate submission.

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns.

Regards,

## Cc: PeckGim.Teo@international.gc.ca; Georgina.Comrie@international.gc.ca

Subject: C11 Entrepreneur with Valid CSQ -

Good day,

To be eligible, a foreign national must have a valid CSQ as an entrepreneur or self-employed person;

early entry;

#### -- IM-2020-0251

2A-2019-16114-000042

IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

The applicant is required to provide either an offer of employment number (i.e. A#######) from the Employer Portal, or, if they are not able to enrol in the Employer Portal because they do not have a CRA business number, they must contact the Employer Portal mailbox to receive the IMM5802 form. When they contact the Employer Portal mailbox, IPG or CEB (Client Experience Branch, who own the Employer Portal mailbox) must include a not indicating that the individual is authorized to use the form. If the note is not there, you may contact the inbox to confirm the situation, or refuse the application. There is a chance that the note was missed/forgotten just due to human error.

The bilateral agreements to do not stipulate that a valid endorsement is required, but rather that the applicant must provide a letter from the province which confirms that the province has received and reviewed a valid endorsement certificate. Therefore, it may actually be expired by the time the work permit application is submitted or reviewed.

That said, we agree that we should not issue work permits to these applicants when their endorsement has expired and their PR applications are returned. The policy intent was to provide a work permit for foreign nationals while they await PR processing. Since this is no longer the case, we agree the purpose of the work permit is no longer valid.

Should these applicants still wish to pursue the AlP pathway, they must start over from the beginning and seek a new

### From: Babb.Marie

# Sent:March 25, 2020 12:05 PM To:Legault.Stephanie

### Cc: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

## Subject:FW: Change of location-LMIA WP -- IM-2020-0279

Good afternoon Stephanie,

My sincere apologies for the delayed response.

It should be noted that there are two sets of conditions imposed under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) – conditions imposed on employers (R209.2) and conditions imposed on temporary foreign workers

## (R185).

Amending the LMIA to reflect the new work location would meet the conditions imposed on the employer in regards to working conditions [R209.2(iii)], however, this does not account for the conditions imposed on the foreign worker in their work permit. As such, if the work permit indicates a specific work location (e.g. in the ADDITIONAL INFORMATION, REMARKS or CONDITIONS sections of the work permit), even if the conditions do not state specifically “not authorized to work at any other location", the foreign worker must obtain a new work permit to match the information reflected in the LMIA before working in a different location.

If there is no location noted (including in the ADDITIONAL INFORMATION or REMARKS section) and no condition imposed regarding location noted on the work permit, then the worker may change locations, but only for the employer specified on the work permit.

Hoping this answers your question and please let me know if you need any further clarification.

## Thank you,

## Subject:RE: CMB Question: T24 - 7 years maximum -- IM-2020-0119 -- DUE 12-Feb-20

## Hello Stefanie,

Please see the answer to your question below.

Question: A client was issued a work permit under T24 (Intra-company transferee, FTA) with a shorter duration than requested because the officer determined that the client had exhausted the maximum number of years (7) of temporary employment in a managerial capacity as per the following instructions (see section 4.9), which say, "Intra-company transferees is the only NAFTA category to have a “cap” imposed on the total duration of employment. The total period of stay for a person employed in an executive or managerial capacity may not exceed seven years." However, of the client's 3 previous work permits, only one was under T24. The first two were under C10 – Significant Benefit. The client believes these should have been excluded from the 7 year calculation.

Can you confirm if prior work permits not under the T24 category should be included in calculations of the 7 year maximum?

Answer: A foreign national's accumulated duration of work in Canada under the Intra-Company Transferee (ICT) category begins on the date of issue of the first work permit issued to the foreign national in this category. Work permits issued under C10-Significant Benefit are not part of the ICT stream.

Note that under these provisions, ICTs are able to work in Canada up to seven years for executives and senior managers, and up to five years for those with specialized knowledge, after which a period of at least one year of full-time employment in the company outside Canada must be completed before being eligible to re-apply to Canada again as an

## ICT.

We hope this information is of assistance.

Best regards,

We have a case (UCI where the client's status was changed from CR to "Not deemed Protected Person", which led to the refusal of the PPAPR (). The officer sent correspondence in error noting that there was an appeal by the Minister – the office has noted that this was done in error and has therefore reopened the application.

Notwithstanding the erroneously sent letter, there appear to be other admissibility concerns from criminal convictions in Canada that would likely render him inadmissible under A36(1). We understand that a protected person may lose status through cessation or vacation, and that a danger opinion under A115(2) (in this case specifically A115(2)(a)) would allow for removal.

Given this, the CPC will be transferring the PPAPR to the local IRCC office for further assessment on inadmissibility.

Could you please advise how the danger opinion would affect the APR and the client's status? It is likely that the final decision on the APR would be refusal based on inadmissibility, however would we be correct in understanding that the client's status remains as a protected person and that the PPAPR should continue being processed, but removal proceedings may still take place before final decision given the danger opinion?

## Subject:

#### IPG Mailbox, please close this request.

Bonjour,

#### Merci pour les questions.

Équité procédurale et correctifs Pour résumer le contexte mentionné dans la demande d’orientation fonctionnelle, des questions d’équité procédurale sont soulevées pour le dossier en question puisque le demandeur était inconscient et hospitalisé lors de l’initiation de l’examen des risques avant renvoi (ERAR) et de la remise de l’avis ERAR par l’Agence des services frontaliers du Canada (ASFC). Une décision négative avait été rendue par un premier agent ERAR en date du 19 août 2019. Cette décision n’a pas encore été remise au demandeur. Pour pallier le doute quant au bris de l’équité procédurale, il sera offert au demandeur de mettre à jour son dossier ERAR à l’intérieur d’un délai de trente jours par une lettre qui lui sera remise en main propre. Une nouvelle décision devra être alors prise par un autre agent en tenant compte de la mise à jour (si éventuellement soumise par le demandeur) puisque l’agent initial au dossier n’est pas disponible et qu’il est en détachement.

Examen des risques avant renvoi par le second agent ERAR Le second agent ERAR devra alors évaluer les éléments de preuve soumis au dossier dans leur ensemble et tirer sa propre conclusion. Il est donc exact de dire qu’il est préférable de ne pas procéder par l’ajout d’un simple addendum lors de l’analyse de l’ensemble du dossier comprenant la mise à jour. Les Instructions sur l’exécution des programmes-IEP [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/service/fairness-equite-fra.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/service/fairness-equite-fra.aspx) indiquent que «dans certaines circonstances, il peut arriver qu’un autre décideur soit nommé responsable de la demande. Ce nouveau décideur doit veiller à évaluer toute l'information au dossier, et il faut indiquer clairement dans les notes que cette évaluation a eu lieu. Lorsqu'un dossier est transféré à un autre décideur, il peut s’avérer nécessaire d’acheminer une nouvelle lettre d’équité procédurale (...). » Il est aussi pertinent de rappeler que : «Chaque demandeur d'ERAR a droit à un examen indépendant complet des faits. » (Voir [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/prra-erar/decisions-fra.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/prra-erar/decisions-fra.aspx))

Considérant aussi qu’il semble y avoir déjà eu manquement à l’exigence de permettre au demandeur de se faire entendre et dans un souci de transparence, il serait très pertinent que ce contexte et les correctifs apportés pour permettre au demandeur de présenter des soumissions et des documents soient consignés et détaillés dans les notes du second agent. Par exemple et à titre indicatif : qui a relevé que la première décision avait été rendue alors que l’ERAR avait été initié alors que le demandeur était inconscient; date d’annulation de la décision initiale et le fait qu’elle n’a aucun impact sur l’évaluation faite par le second agent ERAR; entente prise avec l’ASFC pour permettre au demandeur de soumettre des documents; date de remise de la lettre d’offre de mise à jour / le nom de l’agent qui lui a remise / en présence d’un représentant ou non /si pertinent, les déclarations du demandeur lors de la remise de la lettre; date de réception des soumissions et documents; tout autre fait pertinent.

Aussi, une copie de l’offre de mettre à jour le dossier ERAR devrait être aussi dûment conservée au dossier du demandeur de même que la réponse de celui-ci à ce sujet.

SMGC Quant à ce qui est de la décision et de la lettre initiales datées du 19 août 2019, elles peuvent être annulées dans les systèmes SMGC. Il est important de conserver celles-ci au dossier papier et portant la mention qu’elles ont été «

## annulées » et ce, par souci de transparence et d’équité.

Je confirme que vous pouvez suivre les instructions « Rouvrir la demande ERAR en raison de réouverture – décision par

# encore remise au client) » dans l’AIDE-MÉMOIRE – ERAR dans le SMGC.docx [http://gcdocs2/otcs/cs.exe/properties/68820681](http://gcdocs2/otcs/cs.exe/properties/68820681).

Des notes devraient aussi être ajoutées au SMGC pour expliquer l’annulation de la décision initiale ERAR datée du 19 août 2019. Par la suite, le deuxième agent pourra entrer les résultats de ses propres conclusions suite à son analyse dans SMGC.

## SNGC

Pour le système SNGC, il est possible de « supprimer » l’étape concernant la décision ERAR négative initiale. La décision du second agent ERAR pourra alors y être enregistrée lorsqu’elle sera finalisée. À ce moment, il serait aussi pertinent d’indiquer une brève note dans les observations (« Obs. ») concernant l’annulation de la décision initiale datée du 19

# août 2019 et la lettre d’offre de mise à jour remise au demandeur.

GCDocs La décision initiale du 19 août 2019 devrait être aussi être enlevée et remplacée par la décision du second agent au système GCdocs.

APPLICATION-- IM-2020-0077 -- DUE 4-Feb-20

Good day Anna,

## Thank you for your enquiry.

Program delivery instructions on excluded family members can be found on the IRCC website under the section Family class: Excluded relationships.

As per R125(1)(d), a foreign national is not a member of the family class if they were a non-accompanying family member of the sponsor and were not examined [R5, R117(9)(d), R117(10) and (11) and R125(1)(d), R125(2) and (3)].

Foreign nationals sponsored under the family class may be exempt from paragraph R125 1) d) if they meet the requirements of the temporary public policy. In this case, the sponsor's spouse would have been considered a non-accompanying family member (who was not examined) at the time of the sponsor's application for permanent residence in 2014. The officer may refer to the PDls on the "Pilot program to exempt permanent residence applicants in

## the family class from paragraph R117(9)(d) or R125(1)(d) exclusion" for information on eligibility and admissibility

requirements. Please note that the new public policy would apply in cases where the foreign national, if declared and examined at the time their sponsor immigrated to Canada, would not have made their sponsor ineligible.

If further support is required for this case specific enquiry, please contact CMB Immigration Case Advice / Conseil Cas Immigration DGRC (IRCC)

#### Trusting your concerns have been addressed.

## Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Question:

Seeking information on how the Express Entry online application system works when an applicant declares a CC or PR spouse. Normally when the spouse of a Skilled worker PR applicant is a CC or PR already, information and documentation such as complete personal history and police certificates are not required as the spouse is not being processed with the PA.

A DLl reached out as one of their employees was invited to apply, has a CC spouse and has indicated as such in the online process but the system has requested her complete personal history, family info and police certificates. Is this correct? How would an applicant respond so that their CC spouse does not trigger document requests for examination.

Answer:

Ask that the applicant declare the Canadian spouse as "non-accompanying" and declare them as a Canadian relative. If any documents are requested, upload evidence that they are a Canadian Citizen and a brief explanation.

We trust that this information will assist you.

## Sincerely,

### HI Suzanne

### I do hope all is welll

Thanks that is great to hear. Please note that I have received feedback from stakeholders that C20 reciprocity guidance is being inconsistently applied across different offices and departments. Some reps now have their applicants fly into Vancouver or Toronto in order to obtain a C20 work permit based on the conditions that program guidance below has specifically stated does not meet eligibility: So in this case, the foreign national is an employee of (which fulfils condition #1) but as far as we know, it appears that the officers was not satisfied that condition #2 is met since there is no agreement between to and exchange personnel. Is this correct?

internal processes for a non-reciprocal external process. Rather, the rep is trying to leverage the reciprocity in gets to hire a TFW, but what does get?

Essentially the reps I met with at EY law indicate that they have been successful in obtaining C20 work permits through some offices and through some opinions where company X has PRs and Cad Cits working abroad and they are seeking to bring in a foreign national from Company Y with whom they have not specific reciprocal mobility arrangement. Their argument is that overall the company has people working abroad and therefore should benefit from reciprocity to bring foreign nationals in to work for them even if there is no prior relationship and they are essentially a "new hire".

Here is a specific example: We have historically leveraged the C-20 Reciprocal Benefits category where there are clear mobility provisions and evidence of a higher proportion of Canadians employed abroad compared to foreign nationals in Canada. Our team recently encountered a challenge at the Calgary Airport where despite a positive IMWU opinion (Client ID 1 CBSA took the position that the foreign national was required to be a current employee abroad in order to be eligible. We have seen this feedback intermittently at different ports and without consistency. Calgary seems to have taken a firm position on this.

The current guidance on C-20 does not specify that current employment is required and in fact would limit the utility of the exemption compared to other categories such as intra-company transfers.

ON reviewing the decision, the IMWU officer took the approach that where no past reciprocity exists then a small number of applicants may be approved. The BSO was of the opinion that it was a new hire scenario as it is indicated that coming to work for but quit his job with the applicant in question is not an employee of to work for

This is not the first feedback I have received about a sometimes inconsistent application of C20 for these specific employee mobility circumstances.

#### Subject: FW: ELN-AB Question concerning reciprocal employment -IM-2018-0761- due 14-Sep-18

##### Hi Sarah, (my apologies again for the delay)

##### We consulted with Immigration Branch/Policy team.

In IB's opinion, there are two conditions when an employer choose to hire foreign nationals under the C20/ Reciprocity provision:

#### 1. There must be an existing relationship between the foreign national and the foreign employer/entity.

2. There must be a mutual exchange agreement between the Canadian entity and the foreign entity. Typically, the exchange is mutually beneficial for both parties (otherwise, why enter into an arrangement), and the net effect on the Canadian labour market is neutral.
So in this case, the foreign national is an employee of (which fulfils condition #1) but as far as we know, it appears that the officers was not satisfied that condition #2 is met since there is no agreement betweenand to exchange personnel. Is this correct?

Rather, the rep is trying to leverage the reciprocity in internal processes for a non-reciprocal external process.

#### gets to hire a TFW, but what does get?

I believe the C20 PDls require an update to include the above information about the two conditions. My colleague Amelie Laporte is the lead on C20. I have copied her in my consultations with Immigration Branch.

Hope this helps,

Suzanne Suzanne Dib

## From: Finall.Sarah

Sent: March 9, 2020 5:42 PM To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC) Cc: DN Engagement / Sensibilisation RN (IRCC) Subject: DSC Guidance Request-Authorized Leave and Coronavirus

## Good day IPG

I received some enquiries from one of my DLls and prepared responses. Could you please review the following and advise of any changes/corrections to ensure my guidance is correct:

As you can probably imagine, the Novel Coronavirus has affected many of our students who are completing internships or co-op work terms in China this semester. Our university's International Co-op Office has issued communication to all students (international and domestic) currently in China (on an internship or work term) strongly recommending they return to Canada. I was wondering what the immigration consequences would be if the international students decide to return to Canada. Please see some scenarios and questions below.

Scenario 1:The student is considered to be on an "Authorized Leave" during the spring semester and is reported as such. Would this impact their PGWP eligibility? If yes, is there any documentation the institution could provide for the student so we can remedy this unfortunate circumstance? If the institution considers the student to be on an authorized leave, then the student should provide documentation confirming their leave was authorized with the PGWP application.

Scenario 2:The student is considered to be on an "Authorized Leave" during the 2020 spring term (January-April) but they were scheduled to have a "Academic Break" during the 2020 summer semester (May-August) and will be enrolled in full-time studies during the 2020 fall term (September-December). In order for the summer term to be seen as an "Academic Break" (and consequently, the student would be able to work full-time, if meeting eligibility criteria) the summer break needs to be sandwiched between two full-time academic semesters but due to this unforeseen circumstance, the student does not have a full-time spring term.

How should we advise the affected students if they would like to work during the summer term? Do we mention they can only work during the summer term if they are enrolled in full-time studies and clarify they cannot work off-campus for more than 20 hours per week, if meeting all the work eligibility criteria? Or could the IRCC make any exceptions for their work authorization during the summer semester if they have documentation confirming their term was affected due to the risk of remaining in China during the Novel Coronavirus outbreak? There are not currently any exceptions to allow students to work if they are not enrolled in full-time studies before and after the regularly scheduled break. Students on an authorized leave are not permitted to work and students on a regularly scheduled break following an authorized leave would not be permitted to work. In order to work off campus the student must be enrolled in a program leading to a degree, diploma or certificate. Therefore if a student is taking courses full-time during what is normally their regularly scheduled break and the courses are required for their education credential program then they could possibly work up to 20 hours per week. However if the student enrolls in courses that are not requirements for their program of study or are not full-time in courses for their program of study then it would not appear that the requirements for off-campus employment are met. I will forward your comments concerning exception requests for students who may have had their studies interrupted by the outbreak but currently the normal requirements apply.

Scenario 3:How would it affect the student if he/she was on an "Authorized Leave" during the spring term and then does not have any classes scheduled during the summer break. This means the student's leave would be less than 150 days but if you factor in the summer semester's break in this calculation, it would be more than 150 days. Would this summer break be counted as part of the 150 day leave? If yes, would this

If yes, what documentation would be required from us to assist the student in this scenario? The 150 day period includes any regularly scheduled academic break. The student would have to adjust their status if they wish to remain in Canada beyond 150 days to that of a visitor. If their SP is still valid they can use the same SP to return to studies once they resume.

Our key Units here have looked at the text and it has raised some overarching questions about process which I am will be able to answer from a local knowledge perspective. Please see our questions below, the answers hoping

A) Is the IRCC request letter still actually required? We know from at least one other location in the Network (Singapore) that we were telling clients they needed a request letter from us to be able to get a PC, however on examining further it turned out that this requirement by local authorities had changed a while back.
B) If a request letter from IRCC is still required, we should reflect on what the current letter actually is. It is effectively a fill-in-the-blank dip note into which the client puts their details. Could this be something that we simply provide on our website itself (perhaps not in dip-note format, but otherwise explaining the context). The current letter does not refer to any IRCC file numbers, etc., and is basically a neutral template indicating to Saudi authorities that a PC is needed to
would be in the best position to comment on whether there need to be changes in support a visa application. the text of the letter or whether it still meets needs of local authorities. Currently, the text of the letter is sufficient. The Saudi authorities require the Embassy stamp and signature of the authorised person (MPM) before they will issue the

Immigration, Refugees 1*and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada

s.17 Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act
Lnfomn

PC. A scanned copy of the letter with my stamp and signature could be put on the T drive so offices can send to applicants as is the case with what Abu Dhabi is doing now. The letter has to be in Arabic because most local employees don't read English. The client also fills out their name on the form in order to get the PC issued in their name.

C) Who should clients contact, and when, to get the request? The current instructions are clear enough in terms of permanent resident applicants (it is not required up-front). However, they are less clear once one starts to read the instructions (presumably for TR applicants). Specifically, the instructions as they currently are may be challenging for clients to follow because they are premised on assumptions about place of processing and that applicants would be aware of where their applications are being processed. This is not always evident with e-Apps and with our triage processes. In the end, it might make the most sense to basically say that only Saudi Nationals and foreign nationals lawfully resident in KSA can obtain police clearances in the KSA and that clients will be sent instructions when clearances are required. Alternatively, we could (with the concurrence with Abu and Riyadh) refer all applicants to submit IRCC Web Forms to Riyadh. Riyadh only requests PC's for LS TR workers and since they are in KSA, it is easy for them to obtain. The assumption is if a person was able to leave KSA, chances are they do not have any criminality and even if they do (although no one has seen it yet) they will not be issued a PC. If all processing offices have access to the signed/stamped PC on the T drive this could facilitate obtaining one. However, we are also saying that if you are a non-Saudi citizen without legal status then you don't need to provide a PC because you can't obtain one so offices will have to determine if the applicant can get one or not. Good morning,

I work as an Account Manager with the Dedicated Service Channel (DSC) and was advised that you may the best point of contact. Would you be able to help me interpret the PC instructions for applicants living in Saudi Arabia?

- The instructions seem clear: Do I need to provide a police certificate with my application for permanent residence? No. We will send you a letter requesting a police certificate after you send your Application for Permanent Residence. You must bring that letter when you apply for a police certificate. However, there's room for interpretation: If you are applying at the Canadian Embassy in Abu Dhabi, UAE, you should submit a police certificate with your application. You can contact the visa office for a request letter by completing the IRCC Web form-Abu Dhabi. Please include your immigration file number if you have one. - Riyadh. Please include the file number, the office where you applied and your mailing address.

## Subject:RE: DSC Request-Question on your response to (IM-2020-0223) -- IM-2020-0256

#### Hey Leslie!

Hope I can clarify the guidance provided.

Indeed the endorsement may have expired at the time of officer review, and that is not an issue. The scenario presented by Abu Dhabi was that the endorsement has expired and the PR application had been returned as cancelled/incomplete. The provincial endorsement is considered valid as long as the applicant submits a complete application for permanent residence on or before the expiry date of the endorsement. All endorsements are valid for six

### months after the date of issuance and extensions are not permitted.

Therefore, if the endorsement has now expired, the foreign national cannot reapply for PR. As it would not be possible for them to meet the requirement to apply for PR with an expired endorsement, we feel that there is no purpose to issue a work permit to candidates in that situation. They should begin the process again, seeking a new endorsement.

You are right that there does not need to be a PR application submitted or in progress for a work permit to be issued. I think the way I worded my response has caused confusion. The policy intent is to provide an optional work permit for foreign nationals to begin work in the Atlantic region before they begin the PR process and while awaiting the PR decision.

Hope that helps! Happy to discuss further.

Tracy Griffiths

I was enquiring with Tabitha at the Abu-Dhabi office to clarify a request she made in processing an AlP work permit. We then got to discussing the AIP, as she was unclear about the timing of the endorsement for the AIP and subsequent applications. This was when she reached out to you – her question IM-2020=02223.

We at the DSC were under the impression (and have seen) that the endorsement from the province had to be valid at the time of “application" but could have expired at the time of review. Does the word application in the Ml's include both TR and PR applications?

We were also unaware that there had to be a PR application submitted for a work permit to be issued, and in fact have many candidates here on TR without having started a PR application. We are confident that employer's Offers of employment remain in place throughout the TR and PR process, and if they wish to withdraw they contact us, or go directly to the provinces.

Your response to her (copied below) seems to support the need for an endorsement and PR application, although this does not appear in the PDI's.

### The response she received is below:

“The bilateral agreements to do not stipulate that a valid endorsement is required, but rather that the applicant must provide a letter from the province which confirms that the province has received and reviewed a valid endorsement certificate. Therefore, it may actually be expired by the time the work permit application is submitted or reviewed.

That said, we agree that we should not issue work permits to these applicants when their endorsement has expired and their PR applications are returned. The policy intent was to provide a work permit for foreign nationals while they await PR processing. Since this is no longer the case, we agree the purpose of the work permit is no longer valid.

Should these applicants still wish to pursue the AIP pathway, they must start over from the beginning and seek a

# new endorsement, followed by the work permit and PR process."

Can you please confirm if this response from you enables this particular processing officer to choose not to issue a work permit without a valid endorsement and PR application? Since there isn't anything in the PDI's to this affect, would the officer have to request further proof that the job offer still exists before refusing?

This is what Tabitha did in this situation -- before proceeding, rather than refusing.

Could the PDI's better reflect this scenario so that applicants will be better prepared in the timing of their applications?

Many thanks for your time and attention.

## Subject: RE: Eligibility/Fraud

# Hi all,

Grateful communications to processing offices be sent through HQ rather than to the office directly-removing them from this chain for now as we have a couple additional points to clarify.

We're thinking it would be more appropriate to pass eligibility and continue processing the APR, rather than changing eligibility to review required. The applicant does meet the eligibility requirements. The review required functionality, in terms of workflow, would simply refer the application to a higher level decision-maker; in these cases, that has already happened, and the eligibility component is not what requires review. This would still support not issuing the BOWP, given that applicants must demonstrate they are not inadmissible prior to the issuance of the BOwP; simply being eligible on the APR does not automatically mean the applicant is issued a BOWP.

2A-2019-16114-000110

and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act Lnfomn

Note that there are multiple applications in question here. While we agree on the principle that the BOwP should not be issued, the interoffice verification has been sent to Manila on the APR rather than the BOWP. Manila would not be making the final decision on issuance of the BOWP-that would remain within CN. If there is misrepresentation, A40 on the APR would be done by Manila, however given that it is an interoffice verification rather than a full file transfer the final decision may still take place within CN.

To summarize: APR eligibility would be passed and we would continue processing to admissibility BOwP would not be issued until interoffice verification results are received If no concerns exist with the police certificate, CN to continue processing APR and issue BOWP If there are misrep concerns, Manila would pursue A40 per usual process

Would anyone have any concerns with this approach?

# Thanks,

# Subject: RE: emergency situation

### Hi Imane,

There are no official procedures that I know of and I have not encountered a case here at CPC-O yet. I have seen it overseas and the general rule is that we will try to facilitate any TRV application from a family member wishing to travel to Canada. In the case below, I would have no objection to cancel the visa as long as we have a credible document confirming the death of the applicant.

18. Foreign nationals with an immediate family member who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident are exempt from the ban. ### Subject:RE: Express Entry-UAE work experience-student visas only-IM-2020-0006---due 17-

Jan-20

## Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Answer:

Please note that while there nothing precluding unauthorized experience obtained outside Canada from being counted under EE, due diligence is required in order to assess the genuineness of the experience/employment. The onus would be on the applicant to provide "verifiable" evidence that their experience meets the requirements of the program they are applying for, and that they received (reasonable) wages or commission for the work performed. Generally, in cases of illegal employment, it is difficult for applicants to provide satisfactory/verifiable evidence of the wages/commission they received. In addition, applicants must provide evidence that they had the qualifications for the position/occupation they claimed to have experience in.

Overall, the officer has to be satisfied that applicants claiming to have experience while unauthorized to work meet all the requirements. Officers should also verify the legitimacy of the business/employer.

We trust that this information will assist you.

## Sincerely,

2 I am emailing about a case in file (Canadian Experience Class) wherein the applicant is claiming work experience under a different NOC than their Work Permit NOC (WP NOC is ineligible NOC for the program).

I am curious if this would be considered working in an unauthorized NOC under this work permit, and if this would be an acceptable refusal for a CEC application? I was unable to locate a specific section in the Regulations.

ANSWER

Answer:

Please note that while there nothing precluding unauthorized experience obtained outside Canada from being counted under EE, due diligence is required in order to assess the genuineness of the experience/employment. The onus would be on the applicant to provide “verifiable" evidence that their experience meets the requirements of the program they are applying for, and that they received (reasonable) wages or commission for the work performed. Generally, in cases of illegal employment, it is difficult for applicants to provide satisfactory/verifiable evidence of the wages/commission they received. In addition, applicants must provide evidence that they had the qualifications for the position/occupation they claimed to have experience in.

Overall, the officer has to be satisfied that applicants claiming to have experience while unauthorized to work meet all the requirements. Officers should also verify the legitimacy of the business/employer.

We trust that this information will assist you.

After e-APR, either during processing of the application or at the RFV stage, the client now asks for their spouse to be listed as accompanying. Currently, there is confusion regarding whether or not officers have grounds to re-assess the PA's point to reflect the change of the spouse to accompanying. A case example of this is CN notes that the PDI's ([http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/perm/express/refuse-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/perm/express/refuse-eng.aspx)) state:

To assess an application under section A11.2, a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR. After an e-APR is submitted, an application cannot be refused due to a change in circumstance unless

- the officer determines that the change occurred before the applicant submitted their e- APR and that the change would have caused the applicant to be refused under section A11.2: therefore, the application should be refused under section A11.2; or Can IPG please confirm if this instruction allows for an officer to re-calculate points if they determine the PA intended to bring their spouse as accompanying prior to lock-in? Answer:

The refusal would be pursuant to A11.2. Should the Principal Applicant (PA) wish to have their spouse accompany after lock-in, and this will result in a loss of CRS points that brings them below that of the lowest-ranked candidate in their round of invitations, officers are to be procedurally fair and advise the PA of the potential loss in points should their spouse accompany, and proceed based on the PA's response (i.e., if they still want them to accompany, recalculate the score with the spouse as accompanying and refuse).

We trust that this information will assist you.

For the periods of work experience claimed in the application, all applicants must demonstrate they performed both of the following:

- the actions identified in the initial lead statement of the NOC description; and
- a substantial number of the main duties, including all the essential duties, listed in the NOC description. This means the applicant performed some or all of the main duties, including all the duties that distinguish a particular occupation from any other. For example, duties that begin with “may" in the NOC description are not usually considered to be essential duties. NOC 6322: Cooks can be found here. As this applicant did not provide a valid passport or travel document with their Express Entry (EE) application, it should be rejected pursuant to R10 and the applicant should be advised that this is not a valid travel document to come to Canada.

Palestinians in Lebanon ordinarily have a light blue, “Travel Document for Palestinian Refugees," issued by Lebanon. This is the document they should submit for a permanent resident visa.

I have a few questions for you, which will help me respond to an applicant's concerns, but also help me understand a few things!

1- When applicants create an Express Entry profile, do they expressly indicate which category they want to be considered under, or is this done automatically? 2- If you receive an invitation to apply under one category, ie: CEC – does that mean that your application will ONLY be assessed under the CEC criteria, even if you may meet the requirements for other categories? 3- If you decline an invitation to apply under the CEC, is there a chance that you could later receive an ITA for a FSW application, even if you have declared work experience in Canada? 4- When you create an Express Entry profile, does it specifically ask whether Canadian Work Experience was accumulated while holding legal TR status? I understand that this is a requirement for the CEC work experience. However, if a client had Canadian Work Experience while they were a PR, but then lost their status, would they then need to respond “no" if this is how the question is formulated?

## Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Answer:

1- Applicants do not select which program they wish to be considered under. The Express Entry (EE) system will determine under which programs the applicant may be eligible for based on their answers. Applicants may be eligible for more than one program through EE. If that is the case, they will be invited to apply for one program based on IRCCs program hierarchy order:

1. Canadian Experience Class (CEC),
2. Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP), then
3. Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP).
## For example:

- If they met the criteria for all three programs, the system would send them an invitation to apply for the CEC.
- If they met the criteria for CEC and FSWP, they would also get an invitation to apply under the CEC.
- If they met the criteria for FSWP and FSTP, they would get an invitation to apply under FSWP. 2- Even if they meet the criteria of another category, the applicant can only be assessed as a CEC applicant. 3- If the applicant's declared answers are such that the EE system recognizes that they still meet CEC, and the program hierarchy is the same, they will end up being invited under CEC again. 4- Unfortunately, the system does not ask whether they held TR status which may lead some applicants to believe they qualify when they do not. Should an officer determine that the applicant does not have TR status (which a PR would not have), they may reject that period of work experience (which may lead to a refusal).

CN would like clarification regarding whether an applicant is entitled to CRS points for arranged employment if they cease to have the job offer after lock-in. According to the PDI, the applicant should be entitled the points as the loss of the job offer happened after lock-in:

### However, MI section 29(3) notes:

Loss of offer or inability to perform duties

(3) If the offer referred to in subsection (1) is revoked or ceases to be a qualifying offer of arranged employment or if the foreign national is unable to perform the duties of the employment or is unlikely to agree to perform them, the foreign national is no longer entitled to the points assigned under subsection (1) in respect of that offer and the total number of points assigned to the foreign national under the Comprehensive Ranking System is to be adjusted accordingly. Can IPG please clarify what is the correct course of action in cases such as this?
Good morning Carole,

IPG provides program specific guidance only. As this appears to be an A36/A40 case-specific issue, I have forwarded this request to our Cases and Advice Unit at Case Management Branch.

Thank you for your query. Let me know if you need anything else.

# Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

While it states in Section 29(3) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system that if the offer is revoked the foreign national is no longer entitled to the points, this only applies if the change occurred before the applicant submitted their e-APR, as per section A11.2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

As per the Program Delivery Instructions (PDI), to assess an application under section A11.2, a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR. After an e-APR is submitted, an application cannot be refused due to a change in circumstance unless

- the officer determines that the change occurred before the applicant submitted their e-APR and that the change would have caused the applicant to be refused under section A11.2: therefore, the application should be refused under section A11.2; or
- the change in circumstance means the applicant no longer meets the minimum requirements

Immigration, Refugees Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canada et Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l'accès à l’information

of the program to which they are applying; therefore, the application may still meet the requirements of section A11.2 but can be refused for failing to meet program requirements.

For example, if an applicant loses their job offer before they submit their e-APR but informs IRCC after they submit their e-APR, the job offer loss can be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment.

If, however, an applicant loses the job offer after they submit their e-APR, then informs IRCC of the job offer loss, the job offer loss cannot be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment. However, the change in circumstance may affect whether the applicant still meets the program requirements, for example, arranged employment points for the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) class.

Answer:

Our guidance on this is based on the case law:

1. Rabbani v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) 2020 FC 257
2. Dhaliwal v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 131
3. Ransanz v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness 2015 FC 1109 Takeaways: Case law on “intent to reside" provides guidance on how to approach reviewing
CN would like clarification regarding establishing intent to reside in a province outside evidence. Quebec as per R87.1(1). What would constitute intent on the part of the client to reside outside Quebec? If the officer is not satisfied that the client meets this requirement, is a Officers can consider: PFL required to provide the applicant an opportunity to allay the officer's concerns or can a decision be taken with the information on the application? 1. The applicant's past conduct, present circumstances, and future plans, as best as can be ascertained from the available evidence and context. Regards, 2. The applicant's declarations regarding their intent to reside.

Immigration, Refugees Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canada et Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l'accès à l'information

3. Must closely assess and consider the ties to province of destination which could include: exploration trips, job offers, family in the province and declarations from the applicant on their intent to reside even if this includes at an undefined period of time.
4. Current residence as evidence of a foreign national's intentions, but it cannot be viewed as determinative. Inferences drawn from an assessment of the applicant's degree of establishment in their current residence (i.e.: outside province of intent), should not – in and of itself, and in the face of evidence to the contrary – be taken as determinative of the applicant's intentions.
5. Ties to another province that is not Quebec: family or relatives in that province, level establishment in current province of residence (time spent there, ownership of properties, temporary nature of schooling or work), previous travel, ability and intent to carry out duties of a job offer.
## However officer must also consider following:

1. The Court found there is no requirement for the Applicant to take any steps to prove her intention to live in a province outside Quebec. The Applicant is required only to indicate on the IMMo08 form where they intend to reside. Nowhere does it say that documentation is required to prove this.
2. There is no guidance provided in the Act or the Regulations, nor any policy manuals or bulletins, defining “intend to reside" or setting out what evidence applicants are expected to provide to prove intention. Indeed, until IRCC actually takes issue with an applicant's intentions, a simple confirmation in the immigration application package is sufficient to evidence an intention to settle
3. Given the two points above, the level of PF required in these cases is therefore very high. A request should not be too broad or request that applicant provide evidence of steps taken to reside outside Quebec as this is not a requirement in the Regulations.
4. The Court held that there is no requirement for the Applicant to take up immediate residence in a province outside Quebec (i.e.: assessing the intent within the validity of the visa did not hold-up in Federal Court). We trust that this information will assist you.

It has to be a new nomination on a new profile. They can only do this for 10% of their total allocation. If they go beyond this, they will be using up their allocation.

# Dear

EE has a counter that counts your nominations. It is set to give you all of your allocation plus 10%. The 10% is meant to give you a little space where one applicant requires 2 nominations. In this way, loosely said, you can “reuse" that space without affecting your overall number of allocations.

Once you go over the 10% then, you would be using two allocations spaces for one person, which is not in your interest nor ours. For this reason, we encourage PTs to work with clients to Can you please advise? help this process go smoothly (like encourage complete applications, for example).

### Subject:

[mailbox: please assign a tracking number. Please find response below. Thanks!] Hi Heather, Thank you for your question. Yes a client will need to submit a police certificate from their country of nationality for their second participation. If the police certificate they have for their first participation is not older than six months, they can reuse the same certificate for their second participation. In essence, does the IEC processing office require a new police certificate with each application? Yes we do, as I presume do other lines of business. From how I understand it, each IEC participation is independent from the previous one so a new police certificate will be required. are they able to refer to the police certificates uploaded with previous applications? From an operational perspective, it may be too laborious searching for a police certificate from a client's previous participation, and ensuring that they are still valid, as documents are uploaded to the client's work permit application and not their UCI. In addition, given that if a police certificate is older than 6 months, this would require CN to send a letter to the client requesting a valid police certificate, thereby adding complexity and additional processing to a file.

### Hope this responds to your question.

Best regards,

Hi IPG, An immigration lawyer (: came to me with a quick question about lEC and I'm not 100% sure of the answer. I know it is possible tor a toreign youth who has used all their participations under Canada's Youth Mobility Arrangement (YMA) with their country to get another participation through a Recognized Organization. I the inverse also true? Could a youth from the UK, for example, who's had a working holiday permit through SWAP, then apply for a second working holiday permit directly? I checked the PDIs for any mention of this, but found none ... United Kingdom Applicants are allowed 1 participation under the bilateral agreement. Repeat participations and discontinuance requirements Applicants are eligible to participate through recognized organizations twice in their lifetime. The 2 participations are cumulative among all present, past or future recognized organizations. Repeat category participations through a recognized organization are allowed. Participations that occurred before the 2016 season do not count toward the 2 participations. A previous participation in an lEC country or territory that has a YMA with Canada does not count as a participation with a recognized organization. Therefore, if a foreign national youth has exhausted their allowable participations under the YMA with a specific country or territory, then they may apply through a recognized organization up to the maximum number of lifetime participations. Unlike general IEC applicants, applicants nominated through a recognized organization are not subject to the discontinuance requirement. Thanks! Sincerely / Cordialement,

As you may know, immigration applicants must submit proof of the Canadian educational credential, OR the foreign educational credential along with the ECA report demonstrating its equivalency to a Canadian post- secondary program credential. Points are awarded on the basis of the completed Cdn credentials or ECA reports submitted in support of the immigration application, that result in the highest number of points. In order to be able to assign the correct points to an ECA outcome, the assessment results shown on the ECA report must match one of the outcomes found in the ECA conversion table, which lists the equivalency assessment outcomes and applicable education points. If it does not, their foreign education is not equal to a completed Canadian credential. In the case of First professional university degree or Entry-to-practice professional degree, our website indicates that the field of study must be one of the following: medicine; veterinary medicine; dentistry; podiatry; optometry; law; chiropractic medicine; and pharmacy.

Sulemani.Val From: February 18, 2020 1:17 PM Sent: Pendleton.Meghan; 'Dominik.Viel-Leblanc@international.gc.ca'; To: 'Sylvie.Cote@international.gc.ca' IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC) Cc: (TFW applications) -- IM-2020-0143 -- DUE 19- crew-Subject: Feb-20 Attachments: in British Columbia AW:

QUESTIONS:

1. Please confirm if Section R205(a) (exemption code C14) applies to these workers or if the 45 or so persons can be considered business visitors.
2. If exemption C14 applies, given that the company confirmed not having a branch in Canada, how should the Employer Compliance Fee be paid?
RESPONSES:

1. If these crew members are essential to the production of this, it would be recommended they look at C14 and confirm each of the members meets the eligibility requirements based on their specific job roles/responsibilities. For those that do not meet the C14 requirements, they can then look at Business Visitor under R186(a) or Performing Artists R186(g).
2. The fee will be paid when you are submitting an Offer of Employment through the Employer Portal.
Please see highlighted below. They can apply to the IMWU and receive a response within 14 business days, and then enter with an opinion letter (the officer's opinion is uploaded to GCMS to facilitate entry at POE).

*Take note* For technical issues with the Employer Portal, please contact the Employer Portal Mailbox. Employers should review the Employer Portal Enrolment and User Guides. For employers wishing to hire temporary workers who are outside Canada and from visa-exempt countries who may be exempt from a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or a work permit, you are encouraged to contact the International Mobility Worker Unit to seek an opinion. There are no costs associated with the opinion request. The opinion provided by the IMWU may be considered by the border services officer but will not guarantee that the temporary worker will be exempt from needing an LMIA/ work permit or entry into Canada.

Greetings from Vienna,

We are seeking your guidance regarding the following:

At the beginning of December 2019, the production company contacted the trade section of our embassy in Berlin to request assistance regarding the work permit requirements to film

The original message from our trade colleague reads as following:

Through my local industry network, I was approached by based TV production company regarding their plans for shooting a. in British Columbia in July/August of 2020.

I have offered to make additional connections to the local film scene but it seems that he is already pretty well connected. The company has, however, requested our support in sorting out any issues related to Visa/work permits for the crew and actors who will be involved in the shooting of this project. I have already informed the company that this responsibility is with our colleagues in Vienna and have provided a link outlining the regulations for media crews: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-) citizenship/services/work-canada/permit/temporary/need-work-permit-work.html. had also already sent a request to Vienna with additional questions but only received an automated response with referrals for additional websites.

Given that this project will likely generate approximately € 500.000 in spending for the local film and tourism industry (€

250.000 alone will be spend on accommodating 40 crew members over a period of three weeks) and will have additional tourism promotion impact, I wonder whether VIENN can deal with this client on a preferential basis ensuring that any of lead actors and key crew members can enter Canada seamlessly for filming operations.
was contacted directly to obtain additional information regarding the project. The response is The company attached to this message.

Please confirm if Section R205(a) (exemption code C14) applies to these workers or if the 45 of so persons can be considered business visitors. If exemption C14 applies, given that the company confirmed not having a branch in Canada, how should the Employer Compliance Fee be paid?

Your help with this matter is greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

## Subject:RE: Inquiry-National Occupation Code CEC Refusal Question--IM-2020-0010-due 17-

# Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Question:

I am emailing about a case in file (Canadian Experience Class) wherein the applicant is claiming work experience under a different NOC than their Work Permit NOC (WP NOC is ineligible NOC for the program).

I am curious if this would be considered working in an unauthorized NOC under this work permit, and if this would be an acceptable refusal for a CEC application? I was unable to locate a specific section in the Regulations.

Answer:

Upon review of the applicant's work permit history in Canada, it would appear that they held open work permits with no occupational restriction. Had there been an occupational restriction on the permit, the work would have been considered unauthorized. Occupational restrictions are found in the "Intended Occupation" field for work permits in GCMS.

Should you have concerns with the credibility of the work experience claimed as a result of this discrepancy in job title, you may send a PFL to the applicant.

We trust that this information will assist you.

## Sincerely,

#### Talia Santilli

Program Advisor (Express Entry), Immigration Program Guidance

## Allo Stephanie,

Your advice on the work permit component is correct; however, we would like to add that the new work permit must be approved before the worker can begin to undertake the duties of the new job offer/promotion. If they begin working in the new position before they have the work permit approved, this would be considered non-compliance by the employer.

On the PR component, endorsement is a provincial responsibility and it is their decision in this case not to issue a new endorsement.

The PR application must include IMM5650 and must indicate the job being offered. The job offer and the endorsement certificate in this case would have the same NOC code, just not the same position title. As long as the client meets all program requirements, the fact that the position title on the endorsement certificate and the job offer IMM5650 don't match (but are the same NOC code) shouldn't impact the clients ability to meet the program requirements. It is ultimately up to the officer's discretion to request further information and make a final decision.

I trust this will assist you,

I received the question below from immigration rep. The candidate recently received an endorsement from the province under NOC and job title: 0911 Production Controller. His employer is considering him for a promotion to: Senior Planner 0911. The rep is asking about the repercussions of this change for TR and PR.

In the TR perspective, the candidate would require a new work permit as the job conditions, salary, main duties have changed (which means it would require a new Offer of Employment). Therefore, the work permit would now reflect the "Senior Planner" position.

My question is with the PR process. The endorsement states the former position "Production Controller NOC 0911". According to the rep, the candidate's work experience would be met with either positions. However, I am wondering about the job offer (IMM5650) which offers a one year job offer as a "production controller" which no longer represents reality. Would the applicant require a new endorsement even though the NOC remains the same? The province stated that they would not issue a new endorsement as in their opinion the candidate does not require it (see below).

Can the PR be processed with the old position even though the work permit represents the new position? How would that affect the processing of the PR?

Any clarifications you can provide on that would be much appreciated.

Thank you,

The individual would move from a Production Controller which is a NOC 0911 position to being a Senior Planner which is also a NOC 0911 position as it is still a Manufacturing Manager position.

Liaising with Planning, Engineering, and Material departments to maximize work flow efficiency Generation of Production reports and KPI's Provide input on the overall build strategy, including build plan reviews and lessons learned Prioritizing and organizing in a dynamic environment

The Production Controllers need to have a broad understanding on shipbuilding processes and technical data as well as experience with 3D model software and must have a degree in engineering or a diploma or equivalent experience. The requirements for the Senior Planner are similar and actually require the person to have experience in a planner and/or production environment. The Senior Planner position has a bachelor's degree as a preferred requirement but also requires the ability to read drawings in a new shipbuilding environment. Both positions require experience in a naval shipbuilding setting.

The Senior Planner's duties are to:

Develop implementation plans for all ship Design change for both Design and Production with special attention to the Production cost impact of “out of sequence” work. Work with Engineering, Production Planning and Production personnel at all levels to implement ship Design changes. In Planning Tool build Hierarchal Network of work by Stage of Construction, based on the Assembly planning in the 3D Model, the Production Bill of Materials, and Unit Integration documents. Build Job Pack schedule in accordance with the Integrated Master Schedule and Work Package schedule in Aveva. Assign Resources, to the Skill level, based on allocated budgets, and Norms. Assign Materials to the Jobs, based on the Hierarchal assembly planning, resulting attributes, and assembly content. Produce Job specific Delivery Request List (s) [Pick Lists] Attend / Conduct Change Implementation Review meetings, to review, discuss, amend and approve implementation approach Work Closely with Production Control to feedback any updates/changes to the Job to ensure accurate and timely monitoring and control

Both roles require the application to plan, organize, direct and control the operations of ship manufacturing. Both roles develop and implement plans to use materials efficiently to meet targets and develop schedules and plan an implement changes to production systems and methods of work. All of these are main duties of NOC 0911. Though the senior Planner role is a more senior role, because of the size of the operation we still would consider this a NOC 0 role not a NOC 00 role.

The applicant's permit is expiring on April 14th but we have just posted the Senior Planner role for recruitment. We have active employees in Planner roles (one of whom was just recently endorsed) which would support the assertion that there likely isn't a Canadian for the role, but this is also simply a desire to be able to promote a foreign national who is actively pursuing PR in the same way that a Canadian would be considered for a promotion.
