#### March 11, 2020

#### IPG mailbox : please close the tasking

Bonjour Sylvie, Désolée pour le délai. You are correct that we currently have discussions around soccer players, we may be able to provide further details at a later date.

For now, I believe your assessment is good in the sense that you're satisfied that he is a genuine soccer players but still need to demonstrate reciprocity. Here are some guidance as to what they could provide in terms of evidence:

● Guidance on reciprocity: Acceptable evidence of reciprocity may include: o A copy of the exchange agreement between the Canadian and the foreign leagues. It must be clearly evident that reciprocity exists and Canadians were occupying these positions in other countries; o Proof from the foreign government that Canadian soccer players are allowed to work in the foreign country as athletes and the requirements of the foreign country; o A letter from the Canadian Soccer League that they have players on their teams from many countries (ie: not just this team). o When issuing a subsequent work permit, proof that the athlete played soccer during the season.

Bona fide evidence of reciprocity will allow the officer to issue a work permit. If, upon assessing the information submitted by clients or their representatives, the evidence of reciprocity is not presented to the satisfaction of the officer, the work permit may be refused, or the applicant may be notified that an LMIA must be obtained for further consideration of a work permit.

#### I hope this is helpful.

## Thank you,

Hello Angela,

### Thank you for your inquiry.

Although the information letter sent out was directed specifically at the PGWP, the eligibility to work full-time applies to other work permits.

R186(w) does not specify that the work permit application must be a PGWP. As a result, an applicant can start working full time after submitting their work permit application, provided that they meet the R186(w) requirements.

In addition, the information on the website states that if a student already applied for a work permit after their graduation, they can work full-time if they meet all of these requirements:

They were already able to work off campus during your studies

They're waiting for a decision on your work permit application

>

# To:Vanberkel.Mark

### Cc: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

## Subject:RE: Job aid for cases involving abuse

Good morning Mark, We have finally received all the required information from our partners in order to respond to your inquiry. Question #1 If someone comes to our office seeking a TRP on the grounds that they are subject to abuse of a criminal nature from their employer / spouse – does the officer have discretion with regard to contacting police proactively vs maintaining the client's privacy ? If, to use an example from a PDI, a TRP applicant alleges that their employer made a threat towards them, but they themselves have not nor are inclined to make a complaint to the police, what if anything is the officer's responsibility? And how exposed is the officer / department if they do not inform the police and the employer follows through on the threat?

## Response #1

When an IRCC officer, in the course of carrying out their authorized duties under the IRPA, comes across clear evidence of a crime, they can pass that information on to police without the need for further lawful authority (Quebec (A.G.) v. Laroche, 2002 SCC). This is based on the proposition that no one can reasonably expect that such discovery in the course of doing ones job will be ignored. Note, however, that rather than disclosing the entire immigration file, IRCC would have to restrict the information shared with police to the evidence relating to the suspected criminal activity. Additional authority, such as a court order, would be required to permit greater disclosure or to provide further information to law enforcement if requested during the course of the criminal investigation. Question #2 And how exposed is the officer / department if they do not inform the police and the employer follows through on the threat?

### Response #2

The fact that an immigration officer found that there was abuse does not automatically mean that a criminal offence would be established. Rather, if IRCC provides information to the police regarding suspected criminality, that evidence may be used to explain why a particular criminal investigation was launched. At trial, IRCC may be called on to provide affidavit evidence (noting that the defence technically has the ability to cross-examine the author); however, the extent of IRCC's involvement would really depend on the facts of the particular case and the nature of the information

### provided. Question #3

Is there a mechanism in place to track / record the identity of the alleged abuser in GCMS – to assist in the prevention of further victims? For example, if we receive a credible allegation of abuse from a worker against his employer, or a spouse against his/her sponsor, is there a mechanism to record in GCMS that said employer / sponsor is an abuse risk – so as to avoid future potential victims? Response #3 Our recommendation is for;

1. DN to create an link it to the client's UCl as well as the ORG ID of the employer (if there is one)
2. The referral emailsent to CMB should contain information under the “Any Additional Documentation/Evidence" section informing them whether the enforcement authorities have been contacted and whether has been created in the GCMS.
Please do not hesitate to contact me should you have any questions or concerns about the information above. Thank you again for your patience with this request and have a great day! Regards,

Here's my interpretation (− FYI only):

Members of the armed forces of a country designated for the purposes of the Visiting Forces Act [R188(1)(b)]

Members of the armed forces of a country that is a designated state, for the purposes of the Visiting Forces Act, coming to attend training for a duration longer than 6 months do not require a study permit [R188(1)(b)]. These individuals are also exempt from the requirement of obtaining a temporary resident visa (TRV) or an electronic travel authorization (eTA), per paragraph 296(2)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), and a medical examination, per paragraph R30(1)(d).

2 is NOT a designated state.

However,

"A DLl number was created for foreign nationals who are not exempt under paragraph R188(1)(b) and have been accepted into military educational institutions that are federally administered: Military Educational Institution 0241487822222."

So the nationals who are applying for 10 months of studies at the Canadian Forces Language School DO require Study Permits since the studies are over 6 months. In their applications they should include the above DLl.

# Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ)

If you will study in Quebec, you need a Certificat d’acceptation du Québec (CAQ) issuec the Québec government. Your school can give you all the details on how to apply for CAQ. If you got approved but are waiting to get the CAQ. you can apply for your study per with the approval letter from the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Diversité et de l'Inclu (MIDI). Find out about the process and the documents you need for studying in Quebec.

## Custodian declaration (minor children)

If a minor requires a custodian in Canada, you must have the Custodian Declaration (PDE_102MB) that has two pages that must be notarized (certified by a notary) and included with the study permit application:

- the custodian in Canada must sign the first page and
- the parents or legal guardians of the minor child in the child's home country mu sign the second page.

### Cc: Katz.Miriam; IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

## Subject:RE: JUDICIAL REVIEW (DISMISSED):

- IM-2020-0126 -- DUE 14-Feb-20
## Good Day,

#### Thank you for your email correspondence.

Question:

We received few days ago a court decision on an EE (PV2) application we refused for not meeting A11.2. These decisions are usually taken in Canada but for operational reasons, some applications were still transferred to the mission. It was determined by the judge that

Issue: to date (for PV2s), once A11.2 is met (which is decided in Canada), the PDl states that the application can only be refused if one or more of the following applies:

the applicant does not intend to live in the province that has nominated them the applicant is unlikely to be able to successfully establish economically in Canada the applicant is participating in, or intends to participate in, a passive investment or an immigration-linked investment scheme as defined in subsections R87(5) to R87(9) of the Regulations the applicant has failed to meet the requirements of A11.2 (in the case of applications submitted through Express Entry).

In light of the decision below, it is our understanding that for a PV2 applications, even if ClO decides that the applicant meets A11.2 but when assessing the file, a visa officer is not satisfied that the employment letter provided meets the NOC of the provincial nominee certificate, we can still refuse the file. Can you confirm? If this is the case, a PDI update may be required.

Answer:

An officer at IN can still refuse a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) Express Entry (EE) application if they are not satisfied that it meets all the requirements.

While it is expected that the Case Analyst at ClO (CN) assessed A11.2 correctly, should an officer in the IN not be satisfied that the applicant meets the requirements of A11.2 and/or that they do not meet the Minimum Entry Requirements (MEC)(in this case the FSW requirements), the IN officer may still refuse the application. The decision of the Case Analyst at ClO is not final.

We trust that this information will assist you.

Sincerely,

#### Subject:RE: Minor child (16) enrolled in secondary school-can he work? -- IM-2020-0120 --

DUE 12-Feb-20

Hello Angela,

##### Thank you for the question.

It is correct that all secondary schools are designated learning institutions. However, an international student can only work off campus without a permit if all of the following statements are true:

•they hold a valid study permit •they are full-time students enrolled at a designated learning institution (DLI) •the program in which they are enrolled is a post-secondary academic, vocational or professional training program, or a vocational training program at the secondary level offered in Quebec •the program of study is at least 6 months in duration and leads to a degree, diploma or certificate

More specifically, in regards to your question the FN must meet R186(v)(i), R186(v)(ii) and R186(v)(iii) in order to work without a work permit.

### Thank you

#### Stephen

Hi,

### One of our GSS employers with the following enquiry and requires guidance;

A Temporary Foreign Worker has a son who turned 16 this year. Their employee wants his son to be responsible for things and would like that he be allowed to work part time after school. However, as the child is a minor and enrolled in a secondary school program he does not meet all the eligibility requirements of work off-campus as an international students.

Moreover, as an accompanying child of a temporary foreign worker, they are allowed to study in primary/secondary schools in Canada. We understand from the instructions about the study permit-all secondary schools are designated learning institutions. As the secondary schools are DLI schools as per R211.1, therefore, we believe that the candidate meets R186 (v)(i) and be allowed to have a remark on their study permit to work part time.

Your guidance in this matter is truly appreciated.

## Thank you,

You may or may not be aware that we ran an pilot this December where the bar code on the letters issued to the students was scanned. The documents would then print, by the time the student saw a BSO, the documents would already be printed, which expedited the initial processing. However, as you can see from below, some errors made at the CPC have resulted in students coming back to have corrections made. The recurring issue is the conditions placed on the permit: Conditions:

1. Must leave by 2. This permit does not authorize the holder to engage in off campus employment in Canada
#### Remarks/Observations:

May accept employment only on campus if meeting eligibility criteria per paragraph 186(f); must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria The mistake is happening because the visa office is selecting “Other” as the Field of Study on the permit application in GCMS. This selection does not allow for off-campus employment by default in GCMS. I appreciate that the BSOs should have more closely looked at the document, but given the volumes we experienced, I understand why this didn't happen. Would you please liaise with IRCC on our behalf and remind them to input the correct conditions?

ASFC_GTAR_POD-Dist_Imm_T3_DM <CBSA-ASFC GTAR POD-Dist Imm T3 DM@cbsa-asfc.gc.ca>

Subject: Study Permit Corrections at Side door

Hi everyone,

We have had a few individuals arrive at the Immigration side door for a correction to be made to their study permit. These individuals have all had their permits issued through the CBSA Express Study Permit Project which operated primarily at Terminal 1. The recurring issue is the conditions placed on the permit:

Conditions:

1. Must leave by
2. This permit does not authorize the holder to engage in off campus employment in Canada Remarks/Observations:
May accept employment only on campus if meeting eligibility criteria per paragraph 186(f); must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria

The mistake is happening because the visa office is selecting “Other” as the Field of Study on the permit application in GCMS. This selection does not allow for off-campus employment by default in GCMS.

These conditions do not allow the permit holder to work off campus. It would appear that an error was made by the visa office abroad and will need to be corrected at the Port of Entry as they appear at our office. If a traveller arrives at the side door to advise of an error on their study permit and their program allows them to work off campus (no ESL, EAP etc), please re-issue the document with the correct conditions (18 & 53) and indicate in the remarks that the permit replaces the previous document.

Superintendent Cescon advised that we need to keep a record of all permits that were re-issued at the port of entry because of this error so that it can be reported to IRCC and corrected at the visa posts abroad for future arrivals. Officers are asked to bring the old permit to the Superintendents office so it can be logged. Superintendents, please hold the permits for Superintendent Cescon to collect.

## Thank you,

Chris Brooks # 35379 A/ Superintendent / Passenger Operations District / Toronto Pearson International Airport Greater Toronto Area Region / Canada Border Services Agency / Government of Canada ChrisR.Brooks@cbsa-asfc.gc.ca / Telephone: 905-676-5119 / TTY: 1-866-335-3237

## Subject: RE: Post-Graduate Work Permit-Request for guidance -- IM-2020-0209 -- DUE March

3,2020

#### Hello Brandon,

Thank you for your inquiry. The decision as to whether an applicant is eligible for the Post-Graduation Work Permit Program (PGWPP) is not based only on the applicant's completion of their program of study. Equally important to completing an academic, vocational or professional training program leading to a degree, diploma or certificate, PGWP applicants are required to have maintained full-time student status in Canada. Both requirements are not equivalent and our PDls are strict on the full-time student status. Specifically, the applicant must have maintained full-time student status in Canada during each academic session of the program or programs of study they have completed and submitted as part of their post-graduation work permit application. Exceptions to the full-time status can be made only for authorized leave from studies and part-time status for final academic session. In this case, the student did not attend his classes full-time and the student's leave from studies unauthorized by the DLI. For a leave from studies to be granted as an exception to the full-time studies requirement, the break has to have been authorized by the DLl and the student should be able to present evidence that this was the case.

# Thank you,

## Subject:FW: PT-2020-16 Reuse of Enhanced Certificates -- IM-2020-0347 -- due April 3, 2020

## Hi Chantal,

#### Thank you for your question.

It has to be a new nomination on a new profile. They can only do this for 10% of their total allocation. If they go beyond this, they will be using up their allocation.

Dear

EE has a counter that counts your nominations. It is set to give you all of your allocation plus 10%. The 10% is meant to give you a little space where one applicant requires 2 nominations. In this way, loosely said, you can "reuse" that space without affecting your overall number of allocations.

Once you go over the 10% then, you would be using two allocations spaces for one person, which is not in your interest nor ours. For this reason, we encourage PTs to work with clients to help this process go smoothly (like encourage complete applications, for example).

#### We hope this answers your questions.

#### Tracy Burtt

Bonjour Mylene,

J’aimerais que tu me dise si tu veux que je passe par une autre moyen de communication au lieu de te contacter directement. Je ne veux pas que tu te sente obliger de prendre mes demandes en charges. Si tu veux transférer le mail à quelqu'un d’autre ne te gênes surtout pas.

Toujours pour mon cas d’erreur sur permis de travail.

Je te donne l'ID et je crois que tu seras plus en mesure de comprendre et ou de m’aider. et

Le sujet a obtenu un permis de travail comme opticien. C'est ce qui est inscrit sur le permis de travail.

Hier, il est de retour au bureau pour me demander si c’est possible de changer l'emploi pour assistant opticien ou assistant optométriste. La raison est la suivante : pour occuper l'emploi d'opticien, il doit avoir l'autorisation de l'ordre des opticiens du Québec. Selon c’est dire, l'ordre des opticiens se rencontre une fois tous les 3 mois et il ne sait pas à quand la prochaine rencontre. Comme il veut travailler d'ici à ce qu'une décision soit rendue, il demande s’il peut faire changer son permis de travail pour assistant opticien ou assistant optométriste. Pour moi, ce n’est plus un emploi spécialisé. Donc est-ce qu'il répond toujours à la définition de son permis de travail de travailleur spécialisé, je ne crois pas. S'il répond toujours à la définition de son permis de travail, doit-il y avoir une autre demande à DRHCC pour faire une IMT.

Il est conscient qu'il devra payer des frais car même si il y a reçu son permis de travail pour une année seulement, les changements à venir ne sont plus l'erreur de notre organisation.

Pour ma part, je pense que ce sera aussi long faire la demande de changement et recevoir la réponse que d’attendre d’avoir la réponse de l’ordre des opticiens du Québec. Les délais de traitement sont de 93 jours.

Dis-moi si je suis sur la bonne voie et ce que tu en penses.

NB Je sais que tu es en voyagement. Tu peux me répondre la semaine prochaine.

Merci de ta collaboration et bonne journée

### Bonjour Jenny,

Ci-dessous l'information sur quoi faire dans un cas d’erreur sur un document de résident temporaire valide (info que tu as déjà probablement):

Demande de modification de la Fiche relative au droit d'établissement, de la Confirmation de résidence permanente ou de documents de résident temporaire valides

Trousse : Demande de modification de la fiche relative au droit d'établissement, de la confirmation de résidence

## permanente ou de documents de résident temporaire valides (IMM 5218)

Normalement, la modification se fait lorsqu'il y a une erreur sur aux champs « Employeur », « Profession », « Lieu de travail » du permis de travail et non sur la durée.

Option à considérer mais à valider avec les programmes de l'ASFC et/ou vos procédures internes :

Selon vos procédures internes, une note au SMGC pourrait être mise indiquant qu'il y a eu erreur faite sur la date de validité lors de l’émission du PT initial et que le requérant a été informé de faire une modification de document. Puisqu'il s'agit d'une erreur de l’agent traitant, aucun frais n'est requis. Les documents doivent avoir été téléchargés dans le SMGC démontrant qu'il y a eu erreur lors de l’émission du PT initial.

Autre option, selon votre niveau de délégation et le cas, récupérer le PT, l'annuler et en émettre un nouveau.

Dans ces deux cas, je suggère de valider les procédures internes à l’ASFC.

Bonne journée,

J’ai un client qui est arrivé au Canada comme travailleur, l’ASFC qui a fait son permis de travail, lui a donné une année alors que ses documents indiquait bien 2 ans. Il doit faire une demande pour faire modifier son document et ceux de sa famille.

Lorsque je lui ai imprimé le guide la semaine dernière, celui-ci indiquait qu’il n’y avait aucun frais lorsqu’il s’agit d’une erreur de notre part.

Mon client a communiquer avec une agent d’IRCC et celui-ci lui dit qu’il doit payer des frais de plus de 500.00 pour faire modifier son permis. Qui dit vrai? Est-ce que le client est imputable de nos erreurs?

Je fais des recherches et pour le moment, je ne retrouve pas ce que je veux. ### Je poursuis mes recherches

Bonjour Jenny, Veuillez trouver ci-dessous notre réponse à ta question. Passe une belle journée. Suzanne

Question : Pour obtenir le permis de travail, est-ce que le doit payer les stagiaire selon un taux horaire? Est-ce que la bourse ou un montant forfaitaire peut remplacer le salaire horaire? Réponse : Il y a des cas où les demandeurs au titre d’EIC ne sont pas rémunérés selon un taux horaire dans le cadre de la catégorie Stage coop international. Une bourse ou un montant forfaitaire peut remplacer le salaire horaire. Il faut noter que les demandeurs au titre d’EIC qui ont l’intention de suivre un stage non-rémunéré au Canada dans la catégorie « Stage coop international » pourraient devoir fournir, à la demande de l’agent des services frontaliers, une preuve de fonds à leur arrivée au Canada selon laquelle ils disposent de ressources financières supplémentaires pour couvrir leurs dépenses pendant tout leur séjour.

# Subject:

IPG Mailbox, please close this request. Bonjour Naomy et Julie, Merci pour les questions concernant ces demandes d’examen des risques avant renvoi (ERAR). Selon les courriels ci-dessous concernant les vérifications faites avec l’Agence des services frontaliers (ASFC), celle-ci a confirmé que les demandes ERAR peuvent être traitées. Les questions concernent donc le fait de savoir si l’organisme PRAIDA devrait être impliqué dans le dossier de l’enfant mineur et quelle est la marche à suivre pour le faire. Tout d’abord, vous pouvez consulter les hyperliens suivants concernant les directives données aux décideurs d’IRCC concernant les enfants qui revendiquent le statut de réfugié : IEP : Traitement des demandes d’asile présentées au Canada par des mineurs et

## des personnes vulnérables

IEP:[http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/updates-misesajour/2020/aid-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/updates-misesajour/2020/aid-) abuse-aide-violence-fra.aspx (Aide-mémoire concernant les cas de violence)

Les directives de la CISR sur ce sujet sont aussi pertinentes et peuvent être consultées:

# CISR : Directives numéro 3 du président: Les enfants qui revendiquent le statut de réfugié

CISR : Directives no 8 - Directives sur les procédures concernant les personnes vulnérables qui comparaissent devant la Commission de l'immigration et du statut de réfugié du Canada

Ces différentes directives relèvent que l’intérêt supérieur de l’enfant doit être pris en considération dans le déroulement des procédures de demandes de protection. Aussi, elles relèvent quels indices nous permettent de déterminer si un enfant est à risque (par exemple : les pièces d’identité ou les preuves du lien de filiation sont douteuses). Les IEP (voir [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-) mineurs-fra.aspx) nous rappellent aussi que : « L’enfant qui n’est pas accompagné, ou qui est accompagné ou accueilli par des personnes qui n’en ont pas la garde ou la tutelle légale, est considéré comme étant à risque. Toutefois, les enfants accompagnés par un seul parent sont peut-être aussi à risque. »

2A-2019-16114-000246

mmigration, Refugees Immigration, Réfugiés 1*and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act

s.19(1)L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation Ainsi, l’agent doit être satisfait que le lien de parenté entre l’adulte et l’enfant soit bien réel. Pour ce faire, il peut consulter les Cartables nationaux de documentation de la CISR concernant notamment l’obtention d’un certificat de naissance dans le pays d’origine de l’enfant. Les documents au dossier de l’Agence des services frontaliers du Canada à ce sujet peuvent aussi être consultés (une copie certifiée de ces documents consultés devrait être jointe
au dossier des demandes ERAR). Aussi, des documents supplémentaires quant au lien de filiation pourraient être demandés par l’agent (ex. : traduction du document espagnol, tout document au nom de l’enfant sur lequel le nom du père apparaît, etc.).

De plus, un signalement aux autorités de la protection de la jeunesse pourrait être fait si l’agent estime qu’il y a un risque pour l’enfant. En cas de doute, il est possible de leur demander conseil (voir [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx)) :

« Signalement aux autorités de protection de la jeunesse : exigences en matière de signalement officiel Chaque fois que l’agent estime qu’il y a un risque pour le bien-être d’un enfant mineur, que ce dernier soit ou non accompagné, il doit demander conseil aux autorités provinciales en matière de protection de la jeunesse. Celles-ci ont compétence pour les questions liées à la protection de la jeunesse, et elles enquêtent et prennent les mesures qui s’imposent en la matière. Si un organisme local de protection de la jeunesse refuse d’intervenir, l’agent doit demander que le refus soit consigné par écrit et lui soit envoyé. Chaque bureau doit conserver un registre sur les communications avec les autorités locales de protection de la jeunesse et les résultats obtenus. »

Voir aussi les consignes relatives à la protection des renseignements personnels et signalement aux autorités responsables de la protection de la jeunesse qui sont pertinentes lorsqu'un agent communique avec celles-ci (voir [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx)):

« Sous réserve d’autres lois fédérales, il est prescrit à l’alinéa 8(2)a) de la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels que les renseignements personnels dont dispose un organisme gouvernemental peuvent être divulgués, au cas par cas, à une tierce partie afin d’être utilisés dans le but pour lequel ils ont été recueillis, à condition qu’il existe un lien raisonnable et direct avec le but pour lequel ils ont été recueillis au départ. Il est raisonnable de s’attendre à ce que les autorités du pays d’accueil échangent des renseignements pour assurer la sécurité de l’enfant et pour l’aider en soumettant son cas aux organismes appropriés, par exemple aux autorités responsables de la protection de la jeunesse. On ne doit divulguer que le minimum de renseignements nécessaires pour atteindre l’objectif qui, dans le contexte actuel, est la protection d’un enfant. Lorsque l’agent conclut qu’un enfant peut avoir besoin de protection, il peut divulguer les renseignements personnels de l’enfant à l’organisme de protection de la jeunesse responsable en vertu de l’alinéa 8(2)a) de la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels. »

Une audience pourrait être envisagée par l’agent en présence notamment de questions portant sur la crédibilité du lien de filiation. Vous pouvez vous référer aux IEP et aux documents de la CISR ci-haut mentionnés quant aux accommodements spéciaux qui doivent être pris en pareilles circonstances pour un enfant mineur. Il est important de tenir compte du fait que (voir [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/minors-mineurs-fra.aspx)):

« les enfants ont des besoins différents de ceux des adultes et l’on doit en tenir compte dans la façon d’aborder l’examen. Les enfants peuvent manifester leurs craintes différemment des adultes : ils peuvent ne pas être en mesure d’exprimer leurs craintes ni présenter leur demande d’asile de même façon qu'eux. En outre, ils peuvent avoir été victimes de traite, introduits clandestinement ou enlevés.»

Aussi, vous indiquez que le pays de renvoi pour l’enfant est indiqué comme étant le Considérant que l’enfant n’est pas le pays de renvoi devrait être confirmé avec l’Agence des services frontaliers du Canada, si cela n’a pas déjà été fait.

N’hésitez pas à nous contacter pour toute question ou tout commentaire.

As per the Program Delivery Instructions (PDI), to assess an application under section A11.2, a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR. ##### Hello IPG,

CN would like clarification regarding whether an applicant is entitled to CRS points for arranged employment if they cease to have the job offer after lock-in. According to the PDI, the applicant should be entitled the points as the loss of

### the job offer happened after lock-in:

# Change in circumstance declared after an e-APR has been

submitted

To assess an application under section A112 a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR After an e-APR is submitted an application cannot be refused due to a change in circumstance unless

- the officer determines that the change occurredbefore the applicant submitted their e-APR andthat the change would have caused the applicant to be refused under section A11 2: therefore, the application should be refused under section A11.2; or
- the change in circumstance means the applicant no longer meets the minimum requirements of the program to which they are applying, therefore, the application may still meet the requirements of section A11 2 but can be refused for failing to meet program requirements
For example, if an applicant marnes before they submit their e-APR but informs IRCC of the marriage only after they submit their e-APR, the marriage can be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment

If, however, an applicant maries after they submit their e-APR, then informs IRCC of the marriage, the marriage cannot be taken into account as part of the section A11 2 assessment However, the change in circumstance may affect whether the applicant still meets the program requirements. See below for details.

##### However, MI section 29(3) notes:

Loss of offer or inability to perform duties

(3) If the offer referred to in subsection (1) is revoked orceases to be a qualifying offer of arranged employmentor if the foreign national is unable to perform the duties of the employment or is unlikely to agree to perform them, the foreign national is no longer entitled to the points assigned under subsection (1) in respect of that offer and the total number of points assigned to the foreign national under the Comprehensive Ranking System is to be adjusted accordingly. Can IPG please clarify what is the correct course of action in cases such as this?

#### Subject: FW: Re-determination-IMM-7580-19 -- UCI#

Good morning Alessandro, happy Monday. Question for you in regards to at what point (from ITA to finalization of the

#### application) does the MI apply/not apply? Please see string of e-mails below for fuil context.

It seems that our litigation crew are under the impression that the Mls must be met only between the time of issuance of the invitation letter, and that we have made an error here. Our understanding is that the applicant must meet throughout the processing of the application. In this case the permanent job offer was revoked. Can you please provide some guidance?

Given A11.2 assessment is concerned by changes happening between the Invitation to apply and the submission of the Permanent Residence application, the conditions described in the Mis must be met only between the time of issuance of the invitation letter, and the moment where the application is actually submitted. Changes that occurred after the

2A-2019-16114-000256

submission of the permanent residence application shouldn't trigger a recalculation of the CRS. As perMI29(2)(a)(ii),the offer of employment therefore needs to be valid between 20AUG2019 and the 13SEPT2019 only, which is the case here.

The officer has therefore made a mistake in the application of the IRPA, its regulations, and the Mis.

### IPG Mailbox, please close this request.

### Good day,

### Thank you for your question.

In the case at hand, because of the possibility that the claimant would be inadmissible due to security concerns, a report made under section 44 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) was referred to the Immigration Division for an admissibility hearing on June 12, 2015. The eligibility couldn't therefore be initially determined and the consideration on eligibility was suspended on November 28, 2016.

Since then, the Immigration Division (ID) concluded on December 21, 2016, that the person is inadmissible under section 34 of the /RPA. After that, a deportation order and a Pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA) notice were delivered to him, and he submitted a PRRA application. This former application and the decision on the eligibility considerations are both still pending.

The Program delivery Instructions (PDI) detail the resumption of the eligibility consideration process (for cases

## that were suspended before the claim was referred to the Refugee Protection Division)

([http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/withdrawal-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/canada/processing-traitement/withdrawal-)

retrait-eng.aspx). More explicitly, “once the Immigration Division has made an admissibility determination, or the court has reached its verdict (and no appeal is pending), the officer must resume consideration of eligibility”. This step has not been done yet. À decision related to the admissibility determination should be made accordingly.

The PDI mentions that “it may be necessary to request that the claimant appear in order to complete the eligibility and examination process". In other words, this is a possibility but it's not an obligation to meet the applicant in order to finalize this examination process. In that particular case, we have a clear decision from the Immigration Division in which it was concluded that the person is ineligible under section 34 of the /RPA. A letter related to his ineligibility under section 101(1)f) of the IRPA and an enclosed copy of the decision that was made by the Immigration Division should be sent to the applicant in a short space of time. In that respect, the decision related to the admissibility determination should be logically made before the PRRA officer's decision.

You can refer to the sample letter (Notification of ineligibility under A101(1)f)) attached.

## Good morning,

This ref claim has been suspended since 2016. This is a brief summary:

2012- NSSD assessed that there were reasonable grounds to suspect inadmissibility under A34. 2015- A44 report by CBSA and sent to inquiry 2016-11-18- Ref claim received and suspended because of inquiry 2016-12-21 / deportation order issued at Admissibility Hearing 2017-07-05- PRRA initiated and still in process

Question: Since he has been found inadmissible A34, we still convoke the subject for an interview and find him ineligible under A101(1)(f)? Need confirmation for the field. By the way, FOSS is still mentioned in the PDIs.

## Thank you

Once the Immigration Division has made an admissibility determination, or the court has reached its verdict (and no appeal is pending), the officer must resume consideration of eligibility.

It may be necessary to request that the claimant appear (DOC, 13 KB) (available internally only) in order to complete the eligibility and examination process.

To finalize processing, complete the Eligibility Results (ER) screen in FOSS, and follow the procedures outlined in Finalizing the Case.

Horse Owners Foreign horse Owners that bring their horse(s) in from their home country to race in Canada. Exempt under R186(a) as business visitors Foreign horse Owners that bring their horse(s) in from their home country to race in Canada, and also purchase a horse(s) in Canada. Exempt under R186(a) as business visitors Foreign horse Owners that purchase a horse(s) in Canada to race in Canada. Exempt under R186(a) as business visitors

Horse Trainers Foreign horse Trainers that Train horses that they Own. Exempt under R186(h) Foreign horse Trainers that work exclusively for horse Owners from their home country. Exempt under R186(h) Foreign horse Trainers that Train horses that they Own, and/or work for horse Owners from their home country, and also work for Canadian horse Owners. WP required with LMIA Foreign horse Trainers that only work for Canadian horse Owners. WP required with LMIA

## Jockeys

Foreign Jockeys that work exclusively for horse Owners from their home country. Exempt under R186(h) Foreign Jockeys that work for horse Owners from their home country, and also work for Canadian horse Owners. Work permit required but LMIA exemption under C11 if destined to the western provinces. foreign freelance race jockeys working in western provinces Foreign Jockeys that only work for Canadian horse Owners. Work permit required but LMIA exemption under C11 if destined to the western provinces.

Drivers, (Standardbred Racing), Foreign Drivers that work exclusively for horse Owners from their home country. Exempt under R186(h)

Foreign Drivers that work for horse Owners from their home country, and also work for Canadian horse Owners. WP required with LMIA Foreign Drivers that only work for Canadian Owners. WP required with LMIA

As well, are the rules any different in the case of a “stable" coming in to Canada for a short duration to race a horse with the intent of leaving after the horse has raced. i.e. an Owner and/or Trainer and/or Jockey, (or Driver), show up with a horse to race in one particular race with the intent of leaving the Country again within a few days of the race. ## Subject:RE: Request: Foreign nationals to enter Canada -- IM-2020-0339 -- due April 2, 2020

# Good day,

Thank you for reaching out. We appreciate your patience in these difficult times.

As the situation continues to develop, operational measures have been changing alongside the new information and instructions being delivered daily. We are doing our best to deliver these in a timely fashion. As it stands, IRCC, GAC and CBSA are working together to operationalize the interim order implementing the travel ban that took effect on March

18. Foreign nationals with an immediate family member who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident are exempt from the ban. Under clause 5(d), while the immediate family member does not need to be Canadian citizen or a permanent resident, they do need to meet the definition of an immediate family member as defined in section 3 of the Interim Order. All those who do not meet these requirements will not qualify for travel at this time. Policy discussions are ongoing, so this will evolve, but for now the options are limited for these travellers. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. We will continue to release information on these issues as best we can.
## Thank you,

### IPG-Visitors Team IRCC.IPGVisitorsUnitAdminAdminUnitedesVisiteursOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca

We were contacted by two non-Canadians (mother & daughter, passports) who were supposed to board a flight to Canada this morning to join the grandmother living in Canada (Canadian citizen) who they claimed is severely ill They could not board as they are not exempt from the new entry ban.

→As they do not qualify as “immediate family", and we do not have the instructions/authorisation yet to allow entry to Canada in special cases, we told them that there is nothing we could do at the moment.

Once more information & clear instructions are given concerning clause 5d, we shall reassess their request.

I checked the rep on the ICCRC website and she is a valid representative working in BC.

It is important to note that the EDOs should not be counselling on IRCC requirements and should refer the representatives to the IRCC website for information. The EDO's should only speak to their role in terms of documents required to be able to issue a recommendation. If the Immigration Representative is not able to find an answer to their question on the IRCC website then they can send their question to the Immigration Rep mailbox.

Representative's question: We would like to know whether education credential assessment is required for religious education worker. Currently one job vacancy on your website is Religious Education Worker. We have qualified and motivated candidate for this position and he has religious education, but it is almost impossible to have his religious education assessed. We contacted three assessment organizations about the religious education. One of them said they do not assess religious education, another one said they have never done that before, and the third one did not mention anything about assessing religious education.

Could you please advise where our client can have education credential assessment done for his religious education? If no one can assess his religious education, will be able to apply for the position of Religious Education Worker? Answer:

To apply to the Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot Program (RNiP), candidates must have a high school diploma or post-secondary certificate or degree that is valid and equal to a Canadian equivalent. An Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) is required for all candidates who did not complete their studies in Canada.

# Answer:

Technically, all documents on the doc checklist must be submitted in the application, except those marked as "if applicable". There may be some exceptions such as "work contracts" and "pay stubs" for proof of work experience; we will amend the doc checklist to include “if applicable" for these items and any other items which should be treated as such.

In the meantime, to ensure that we are returning/rejecting the right applications, can CiO provide the reasons the application may be returned/rejected to IPG (myself and Nathalie) before taking action on the file. As volumes are low, we can use this exercise to ensure the quality of our decisions.

### Subject: RE: student fraud -- (IM-2020-0124) -- IM-2020-0259 -- DUE March 13, 2020

## Hello,

Please see my approved response below. After contacting Service Canada we were advised that SINs that begin with the number “9” are issued to temporary workers/students such as International students. Employers can therefore easily recognize that a new employee is a temporary resident in Canada.

The SIN will remain the same unless the status of the student changes to becoming a permanent resident, in which case the student can apply for a new SIN which will start by a regular number (not with the number '9.’) SIN numbers associated with coop work permit and study permits do in fact have an expiry date on them. Please see the link provided for more information: [https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-) development/services/sin.html

## Regards,

# Hello,

We are seeking clarification and a standardized approach across the network as well as in accordance with CBSA

## guidelines and concerns regarding operational instruction Study permits: Final decisions.

CBSA have flagged their concerns of the current procedure: We are issuing eTA entry doc for visa required nationals (no instructions/OB could be found online regarding this)

They are suggesting to use the “Not Required” entry doc instead They would like to see the S-1 coded visa from clients as purpose of visit is to study not visit

There has been some inconsistencies when applying these procedures: CPCO SP Iran team: when client holds a V-1 counterfoil valid longer than studies, they are issuing study permit without a second visa, while using the eTA as the Entry Doc. The reason for the eTA prompting was used as an administrative function in order for file to Close (the client is not notified of an eTA approval) CPCO India SP and North America SP: in cases where the client holds a V-1 valid longer than studies, they have retreated from these guidelines and have been issuing the S-1 counterfoil (and affixing a second counterfoil in the passport) --- as instructed by the mission.

Context: As per Operational Instruction, if client holds a pre-existing TRV (e.g. V-1) valid for a period longer than the period of the study permit, it is not necessary to affix a second counterfoil to the passport with the coding S-1 (causing confusion at POE). To do so, we uncheck the Counterfoil checkbox and Entry Doc would revert to eTA. We recently discovered (see below) that the proper Entry Doc could be likely changed to Not Required to avoid the eTA being generated (as this as well was causing issues at POE).

11 Entry Doc: Not Required 2 Entry Doc: eTA 8

# Counterfoil Req:

Counterfoil Req: V

[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/temporary-residents/study-permits/final-decisions.html

Please see attached and below for additional information.

## Regards,

#### Nathalie Lafleur

#### Supervisor CPC-O, Centralized Network

Subject: VISA/ETA occurrences

## Good Morning,

I am just writing to you in regards to client UCI: This particular client is an Indian national, only has Indian citizenship, is not a citizen of Canada or the United States, nor does he hold permanent residence to the United States.

The client arrived at Toronto Pearson International Airport Terminal 1. The client arrived to receive his study permit for his studies in. In the client's study permit application, he has the necessary permit, but instead of a counterfoil, which is required for Indian nationals, he was issued an ETA. The office that was responsible for this application was disseminated by DEHLl to CPC Ottawa.

This is not the only client that I am aware of that has had this kind of issue. Last week, I was asked to help a fellow BSO who also had an Indian national who was also given an eta instead of a study visa. In both cases, the clients had V-1 visas for Canada from applications made prior to their application for study. In both cases, the client's were issued an ETA instead of a study visa, and the study applications were finalized by CPC Ottawa. In the case of the client last week, he had a cancelled study permit and visa in the same application as his issued permit and eta (cancelled and re- authorized by CPC Ottawa).

In the case of my client, he has no friend's or family in Canada and does not currently have a residing address in Canada as of yet. Unfortunately, we will not be able to get a hold of him directly.

I am writing in hopes that you will be able to help rectify these occurrences. As per SOP's I was able to issue the client his study permit as he had all the necessary documents and he was not trying to circumvent immigration laws. However, the issue will come when he tries leaves to Canada and tries to return with a valid study permit but no visa. We are limited by what we can do here at the port of entry and are unable to issue visas. I am hoping that the information can be passed along to the appropriate people to prevent further applications from being processed wherein visas that are needing to be issued are actually being issued.

## Subject:RE: SUV program online -- IM-2020-0319 -- due March 25, 2020

### Good afternoon Leslie,

No particular parameters exist in our PDl's regarding remote incubation programs as in the case you presented. Remote incubation programs are not restricted under the Start-up Visa program regulations either. However, during your assessment of the application I would recommend to place applicant/DE to explain why the services need to be applied remotely on a temporary basis. The processing officers normally pay particular attention to the services the applicant will receive from the DE and evaluate if these seem reasonable to be exercised remotely. If the SUV processing officer perceives clarifications might be needed regarding the viability of those services to be

### delivered online, then the officer will request the applicant the appropriate questions.

Now, regarding the exceptional circumstances regarding COVID, I think officers will understand why, on a temporary and limited basis, these services need to be provided online. Then again, it depends for how long are this exceptional circumstances will be in place and it if the temporary measures of the services match the time frame of the measures taking under COVID. In other words, it should be a temporary way for Spring to provide services.

### Hope this information helps,

## Thank you,

### Cc: IPG Visitors Unit Admin / Admin Unite des Visiteurs OPI (IRCC); Maxwell.Ryan

FW: UN Laissez Passer-Visit of

## Subject:

Importance:High

#### Hi Imane,

Generally speaking, a client with a UN laissez-passer (UNLP)is not eligible to apply for an eTA as the UNLP is not an acceptable document to travel to, and enter, Canada. However, IPG is of the opinion that this client should be facilitated as much as possible given his role and in the interest of maintaining good relationships. Therefore, if the client is eligible for an eTA with their national passport, there is no requirement for the individual to apply for and obtain a TRV as this only causes additional delays and potential for difficulties in travelling to Canada. The UN diplomat should be issued the eTA with his UNLP. I trust that this is helpful,

## Tracey

This is not a new requirement. This is a screen shot of the manual FW1 dated 2014. Under section 5.38 of the manual, the same guidance is included:

### FW 1 Temporary Foreign Worker Guidelines

an official letter of employment from the university written on university letterhead and signed by a senior administrator (e.g. the Program Manager) from the Postgraduate Medical Office. detailing: 0 the position being offered including the area of specialty. if applicable: 0the length of the residency training/fellowship period (number of months) including the beginning and end dates of the residency or fellowship period: the work location(s) for the duration of residency/fellowship: 0 0 the annual income offered to the foreign national with an attestation that the wage is commensurate with that of a Canadian performing the same duties in the same location of work: and that the income offered to the foreign worker is not Canadian-publicly-funded; 0 whether the position is covered by a collective agreement; and 0whether the physician must be licensed by the provincial College of Physicians and Surgeons in order to undergo their residency or fellowship in that province.

Officers may also receive a copy of the letter of eligibility for licensure from the relevant provincial College of Physicians and Surgeons. where applicable. If the foreign medical resident or fellow does not require licensure from the regulatory body, the university should indicate this in their letter of employment. Publicly funded health care is financed with general revenue raised through federal, provincial and territorial taxation, such as personal and corporate taxes, sales taxes, payroll levies and other revenue. Based on the above, the Provincial Public Health Services is publicly funded; therefore, the applicant cannot

## benefit from the medical fellow LMIA-exemption.

Hope this helps,

Good day Sonam and Sylvie,

2011. For personal reasons the client has a applied to renounce his PR status and provided all the necessary documentation (documents have been uploaded to application). The renunciation was approved as everything looked in order, however, after reviewing the PDI for Renouncing permanent residence under the section Protected Persons wishing to renounce their permanent residence states that “A protected person seeking to renounce their permanent resident status should be counselled by the office processing the application on the impact of renouncing permanent resident status (i.e., the possibility of not being able to return to Canada if they leave)." This information can also be found on the Canada.ca website, which is what the client has access to under the section Protected persons wishing to renounce their permanent residence. As to properly process the client's application and following the PDI guidelines and with OSC as the processing office, could you please advise how to counsel the client? Hello Sarah,

#### Sorry for the late response.

In order for a temporary resident to have “implied status”, they must remind in Canada until the decision on their application is made as per R186(6). It is in line with other TR line of business such as SP and WP holders. When a foreign nation re-enters Canada, a new visitor record will be issued by a migration officer at POE. If an officer put a remark indicating that exchange student status in the new visitor record, the foreign national in question may continuous to study.

Can you please provide me the name of the individual and the UCi? I will look into it.

# Thank you.

From: Lau.Stephen Sent: January 8, 2020 3:02 PM To: Finall.Sarah <Sarah.Finall@cic.gc.ca> Cc: IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC) <IRCC.IPGStudentUnitAdmin- AdminUnitedesetudiantsOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca>; IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC) <IRCC.IPGFunctionalGuidance-OrientationFonctionnelleOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca> Subject: RE: Urgent Request-DSC student enquiry-Exchange Students and R215(1)(f)--IM-2020-0024--due Urgent

Hello Sarah,

You are correct that exchange students can apply for a study permit from within Canada. However, please note that R189 (the authority to study without a study permit unti a decision is made on their study permit application) does not apply to this scenario because the applicant is switching from visitor to student. The foreign national is not applying under R217(1) to renew their study permit but is making an initial application for study permit. With the exception of exchange programs, even if foreign nationals plan to study for 6 months or less, if the course or program is longer than 6 months, they need a study permit. Therefore, the foreign nation may not continue their studies with their visitor status until their SP application is granted

An operational reminder was posted on December 23, 2019 (see below). I think it would be a “best practice” for exchange students to apply for a study permit before coming to Canada or to apply for one upon arrival, regardless they are staying for less than 6 months or longer. So that they can apply for a SP extension and benefit from the "implied status and travelling outside Canada".

Monday, December 23rd, 2019 – Operational Reminder: On and off campus work authorizations for post-secondary exchange students

This is a reminder to all Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) officers to include the appropriate work authorization remarks and conditions when issuing a study permit to post-secondary exchange students.

While post-secondary exchange students whose length of stay is less than 6 months do not require a study permit, they may still apply for one if they want to work on-campus [R188(2)].

By obtaining a study permit, these students will be able to apply for a study permit extension from

# within Canada should they wish to continue their studies at a designated learning institution (DLI).

For programs of 6 months or longer in duration, exchange students must apply for a study permit and are eligible to work off campus, provided that they meet all other eligibility requirements of R186(v). Officers must consider the overall program length rather than the length of their exchange with regards to R186(v)(ii), which requires the program to be more than 6 months in duration.

Exchange students remain subject to all normal conditions, notably that they may only work for up to 20 hours per week during academic terms

Stephen Stephen Lau

## Sent: January 8, 2020 12:20 PM

To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

## Subject: Urgent Request-DSC student enquiry-Exchange Students and R215(1)(f)

Importance: High

## Good day IPG

I have an information request from a DLl that they have requested be answered urgently if at all possible as they have students awaiting a response before they can resume their classes. Recent guidance allows for exchange students to apply for an SP from within Canada if they were already studying here as a visitor pursuant to R215(1)(f)(ii). Furthermore, the guidance advise: Foreign nationals who are in Canada as visitors and are authorized to apply for a study permit from within Canada under section R215(1)(f) may begin their studies once they have submitted their study permit application, provided the application has been submitted before the expiry of their visitor status. They are required to cease studying if their study permit application is refused.

Could you advise of the implications of a student who applies for an SP within Canada prior to the expiry of their visitor status, however departs Canada prior to the decision on the SP application and then returns to Canada and is admitted at the POE as a visitor. Will they be able to continue their studies as technically they submitted their SP application prior to the expiry of the initial visitor status, are re-admitted with valid status as a visitor and as per the guidance above may continue their studies with visitor status as long as an SP application is in process?

The DLI in question has students that against their advice went home for Christmas leave and now the institution wishes to ensure they may legally resume studies.

### Your assistance is greatly appreciated.

## Sarah

## Subject: RE:-- IM-2020-0074 -- DUE 30-Jan-20

Hi

In terms of a potential work permit exemption for this scenario, the following category under Work Permit exemptions (work without a permit- section R186) seems like a match:

#### “Business visitors – includes self-funded researchers

Foreign nationals engaged in self-funded research or observational internships (job shadowing) may fall under

### the business visitor category, which could include “research and design” activities for those conducting

independent research or research for a foreign entity. There should be no displacement of Canadian or permanent resident workers, nor should there be any employer-employee relationship. In addition, the

### individual or the Canadian institution must not receive remuneration for the research."

Application:

This letter refers to your application for a work permit.

Based on your application and accompanying documentation that you have provided, I have carefully considered all information and I am not satisfied that you meet the requirements of the

## Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations. Your application as requested is

therefore refused.

## [X] To be eligible to apply for a 1-year employer-specific work permit under the Atlantic

## immigration Pilot Program, the foreign national must submit the following:

### Official language proficiency:

- a copy of a language test approved by IRCC that shows the applicant meets the minimum language level of 4 in the Canadian Language Benchmarks in English or the Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens in French for each of the 4 language skil areas, and the test results must be less than 2 years old on the date of application
Education: Applicants must demonstrate they have either of the following:

- a Canadian secondary (high school) or post-secondary certificate, diploma or degree
- a completed foreign credential
In addition to either of the above, the applicant must have an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) report from an agency approved by IRCC.

- The report must show the foreign education is equal to a completed Canadian secondary (high school) or post-secondary certificate, diploma or degree. The ECA must be less than 5 years old at the time of the application.
#### Qualifying work experience:

Applicants must demonstrate that they have obtained work experience

for at least 1 year (1,560 hours total / 30 hours per week), non-continuous, full-time or an

### equal amount in part-time, within the last 3 years

that was for paid work (volunteer work and unpaid internships do not count) in an occupation with the following National Occupational Classification (NOC)

Create an account to get more detailed application status and your mail online. Find out how: [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/my_application/link.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/my_application/link.asp).

## When should I contact CIC?

You must notify Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC) of any changes to your application. Examples of changes include:

Changes in your personal circumstances, such as birth or adoption of a child, death of a family member, a marriage or a divorce; Change of contact information (e-mail, mailing address, telephone number); Appointment or change of immigration representative or designated individual; Decision to withdraw your application.

Changes to your address should be made through our online service at www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/change-address.asp.

Link your paper application to your online account

Hello IPG,

I am writing from the Abu Dhabi mission with another question concerning the International Mobility work permit stream, this time requesting clarity about the processing of work permit applications under T13.

We have recently received TFWP applications wherein the provincial nominations have expired and the applicant does not appear to have submitted either an express entry profile or submitted a PV2 for permanent residency. We have reviewed the PDIs, in particular the section highlighted below, however are seeking clarification from IPG about the correct procedure to review these applications. For now, we are following the PDls and requesting a “copy of the acknowledgement lettering confirming that IRCC received a PNP permanent resident application" however in the application numbers below they will not most likely not be able to provide this. The question is: if applicants are unable to provide this letter, are we in a position to refuse them as they have not met the provisions of T13 for foreign workers nominated by a province or territory?

### Two examples of files recently seen:

## From PDI:

Note:It is not necessary for the foreign national's application for permanent residence to have been received by IRCC

for the work permit to be issued, unless the nomination is expired. In that case, a copy of the acknowledgement letter

## confirming that IRCC received a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) permanent residence application should be provided

with the work permit application. Officers should verify the PNP application in the Global Case Management System (GCMS) to ensure that the nomination has not been withdrawn by the province and that no adverse information is found on the file.

Many thanks once again for your kind assistance,

6.2 Annex B – Instructions for Entrust ID Instructions for External Subscribers of an Entrust ID (myKEY) Introduction: Documents and emails containing sensitive information about applicants and/or their businesses are classified as protected information and can only be sent via a secure network.
### Microsoft Outlook is the primary tool used to share protected information between external

### parties, and as such, all parties should use the Government of Canada's Entrust encryption

software with their myKEY certificate to share sensitive information.

Individuals identified to manage the sharing of protected information with Immigration, Refugee and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) will need to apply as an external subscriber for a myKEY.

Procedure:

1. Download the External Subscriber myKEY Administration form.
### 2. The form must be filled out electronically, printed and signed by the subscriber and

the guarantor before it is scanned and sent to Immigration Program Guidance (IPG)

### at IRCC. The following sections will need to be completed in order for IT to

process the request:

### a. Section 1: Read the ICM myKEY Terms and Conditions of Use and sign

and date;

b. Section 2: Complete the myKEY Subscriber Information and ensure that all names and details are spelled correctly.
c. Section 4: Your supervisor will need to complete the Guarantor Information section, verify two (2) pieces of ID*, and sign the form.
# d. Section 6: Indicate which action is being requested (i.e. Create, Change,

Recover/Re-Issue, or Revoke). For first time users, please select "Create". If you are renewing your myKEY, please select "Re-issue". Note: you will not require a hardware token.

Note: IPG (IRCC) will complete Section 3 (Sponsor Information) and IRCC's IT

unit will complete Section 5 (Local Registration Authority Information).

### 3. Once you've completed all required sections, please scan and email to IPG (IRCC)

IRCC.IPGFunctionalGuidance-OrientationFonctionnelleOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca for further action.

IRCC Commitment:

IPG will sponsor the form if all has been met and will forward the form to the IRCC IT team for their action. It could take up to 10 business days for this request to be actioned.

Important: You will receive a Reference Number via e-mail message from SSCICMKMC.SPCGJICGC@ssc-spc.gc.ca and EIAM will contact you with the authorization code, and final instructions for the creation or recovery of your myKEY profile.

You will need both the authorization code and reference number to create or recover your myKEY profile using the Entrust software. It is critical that you keep your authorization code and reference number confidential. Once the myKEY profile has been created, you will then be able to send the sensitive information or Commitment Certificate and supporting documents to IRCC in a secure fashion, encrypted with the Entrust software.

The installation of the Entrust software must be performed by your technical support from your organization.

## Subject:RE: Change of sex or gender identifier -- IM-2020-0230 -- DUE March 6, 2020

Hi Mary-Ann,

For the temporary residence line of business, the sex or gender identifier on the client's IRCC document must reflect what is indicated on their foreign passport.

If a client's existing documentation does not specify a sex other than F or M, but they indicate on the application that they identify as X, the client should be informed that the sex or gender identifier on their IRCC document must reflect what is indicated on their foreign passport.

As for your following up questions on which processing level is appropriate for assessing the request and how to notify the client of the decision, I will leave that to CN to confirm as these questions are specific to processing.

1. Which processing level is appropriate for requesting and/or assessing the Request Form for a Change of Sex or Gender Identifier (PDF, 1.8 MB)? ## Sent:

Legault.Stephanie To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC); IPG Student Unit Cc: Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC) RE: Co-op Students-work conditions -- IM-2020-0082 -- DUE 6-Feb-20

# Subject:

Hello Stéphanie,

### Thank you for the questions.

In terms of duration of the work terms, there is no parameters that need to be followed. Student may work 4, 6, 8 months at a time or 10 hours per week throughout the whole program of study, as long as the co-op work is no more than 50% of the total program of study. Also, the guidelines are written in such a way is to provide processing officers with flexibility in evaluating each unique coop work permit application based on the information provided by the applicant and the DLI (ie: Letter of Ācceptance). For example, a 4-year undergraduate degree program with two coop terms (ie: 4 months per term), it would make sense to calculate the ratio using the period of time in days/months. However, for an 8 months certificate program with a 2-month coop, it would be necessary to look into the total classroom time versus the total coop time in hours to ensure the internship employment does not form more than 50 percent of the total program of study.

As per the co-work permit PD, the DLI is listed as employer on the co-op work permit. Therefore, the school has the authority to decide which internship employment is acceptable based on the program of study in which the student is enrolled. It should also be noted that whether a co-op work is paid or unpaid, it is up to the DLl and the employer of the workplace.

Finally, Students PDI, including co-op, is also posted on the department's website as a courtesy to stakeholders.

# Stephen

# Good day,

On March 3rd we received the confirmation from DGO that:

“applicant that sends in an enquiry stating that they are unable to travel due to the Coronavirus situation will automatically be granted and additional 90 days to either comply with required documents, biometrics or travel to

# Canada."

As of that date, we have been automatically granting an extension of 90 days to lEC applicants who informed us through the MAILBOX that they were unable to travel to Canada before the expiration date of their Letter of Invitation (LOI).

What is problematic is that those requests come from lEC participating countries that have medical requirements; meaning that an upfront medical examination must be completed before arrival.

Consequently, in order to proceed with the extension, we would have to make sure that their medicals are valid until the end of the validity date of their new LOI.

Good day Sarah,

I hope this message finds you well. Thank you for your email. Nigeria Student Express is a separate initiative from the Student Direct Stream.

As this is an initiative ran out of the IN missions and a pilot project at this time there are not plans to publish program delivery instructions. However, I can provide you with the below information regarding Nigeria Student Express we have received from our International Network colleagues.

Nigeria Student Express' objective is to improve processing times for study permit applicants in Nigeria by giving them the option to use a secure financial verification system, MyBank. MyBank is available through the principal commercial banks in Nigeria and will assist applicants in demonstrating that they have sufficient funds to cover expenses related to their studies in Canada.

### Applicants are currently expected to demonstrate that they have sufficient funds for their

studies; however, oftentimes, they do not have a means to do so in a satisfactory way, which can slow down processing or lead to a refusal. Ultimately, the goal of the pilot is to allow

2A-2019-16114-000367

Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada mation disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Nigerian study permit applicants to demonstrate that they have the financial means to support their studies.

At this time, those who have a letter of acceptance from a Canadian Designated Learning Institution for a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree program, or for other graduate-level studies, can apply. Given that this is a pilot, it currently focuses on a restricted group of students and includes a solid financial requirement. The criteria for the pilot will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. In addition, students destined to other programs may choose the MyBank option to demonstrate their funds; however, they will be outside the current scope of the pilot.

The initiative has just been introduced; therefore, it is too early to predict how many students will choose this option. By the same token, it is difficult to say how this will affect approval rates; however, as with all other changes made to IRCC processes or requirements, we would encourage DLls to focus recruitment on applicants who would meet the requirements of the pilot. IRCC will continue to evaluate the pilot in coming months.

Should you have additional questions or concerns related to the pilot, International Network who are managing this pilot will be able to respond.

Best regards,

Good day IPG

I just saw this in the daily media calls: Nigeria Student Express is a pilot initiative aimed at improving processing times for study permit applicants in Nigeria. It was introduced to prospective students and their parents at the EduCanada fairs in Abuja and Lagos in January 2020. With NSE, prospective students who have a letter of admission for a Bachelor, Master's or PhD degree program, or other graduate-level studies, at a Canadian designated learning institution may apply using a secure financial verification system, MyBank, to show that they have sufficient funds for their studies in Canada. MyBank is available from the principal commercial banks in Nigeria. Prospective students in Nigeria can apply online as soon as they have the required documents. As the initiative has just been launched, it is too early to tell how many students will choose this option. We will continue to evaluate the success of the pilot in coming months.

Are there PDIs for this initiative? Could you clarify why this was designed separately from SDS?

## Thank you

Work experience does not need to be continuous to qualify and can be accumulated within the last 3 years. When calculating the period of 12 months of required employment, it cannot include any extended breaks in employment,

## Subject:RE: Entry Requirement-American Guest Speaker

#### Hi Eleana,

Please see the answers to your questions below.

Question 1: Seeking clarification regarding Entry requirements of US citizens to deliver an academic presentation to Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC). We are looking at the possibility of inviting an expert guest academic speaker, a professor from an American University, to deliver a presentation pertaining to the agri-food sector. The duration of stay in Canada should be less than 5 days

## as the Presentation itself would last approximately 2 hours on one day.

I don't know if there are any specific agreement between Canada and the US, but I understand that our International American Speaker may be admitted to Canada without a work permit under Regulations 186(j) as a guest speaker. Consequently, AAFC would not need to pay any compliance fee for this speaker. Could you please confirm this is correct?

Answer: That is correct. Section R186(¿) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) as well as our online guidance specify that foreign nationals coming to Canada as a guest speaker (such as an academic speaker at a university) for less than five days for the sole purpose of making a speech may work in Canada without a work permit. The scenario described in your question would appear to qualify under R186(j) and the American speaker may not require a work permit or the payment of compliance fees.

Question 2: Could you also advise if there is anything we would need to file or procedure we would need to follow to ensure the American speaker is granted entry without any issues?

Answer: The foreign national would need to satisfy the Border Services Officer upon arrival of their participation at the

### presentation and that they meet eligibility and admissibility requirements.

In terms of documentation, the foreign national may provide a letter of invitation from the organization, a C.V., and/or any other documents that would help demonstrate to the officer that the foreign national meets the requirements for R186(j) exemption.

We hope this information is of assistance.

### Best regards,

#### Marcia Thaine

## Subject:FW: Foreign Embassies questions-COVID-19 related issues

Bonjour Gabrielle et merci de votre patience.

Veuillez noter que l'Arrêté en conseil dispense les étrangers qui sont exemptés de l'obligation d'obtenir un visa de résident temporaire en vertu de l'alinéa 190 (2) a) du Règlement sur l'immigration et la protection des réfugiés (diplomates accrédités) et les membres de leur famille immédiate des restrictions de voyage.

De plus, pour les résidents temporaires qui sont actuellement au Canada, nous recommandons de faire une demande en ligne pour une prolongation de leur statut. Le fait de demander une prolongation au Canada permettra aux candidats d'être considérés sous un statut juridique implicite. Un lien vers les formulaires de demande requis se trouve ci-dessous.

[https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-citoyennete/services/demande/compte.html](https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-citoyennete/services/demande/compte.html)

Les informations les plus récentes concernant les mesures spéciales prises par IRCC pour faire face à la crise du COVID- 19 sont disponibles en suivant le lien ci-dessous :

[https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-citoyennete/services/coronavirus-covid19.html](https://www.canada.ca/fr/immigration-refugies-citoyennete/services/coronavirus-covid19.html)

### Merci beaucoup.
