Bonjour Mylène, Mes excuses pour la réponse tardive. La question est difficile, parce que nous peu d’information sur le contenu des cours de français en milieu de travail et ne savons pas qui sera responsable de donner cette formation. J’ai écrit à mon contact du MIFl pour avoir plus d’information sur le programme, pour savoir notamment si les étudiants devront fréquenter un EED pour être éligible, s'il recevront un CAQ pour les cours de francisation, si les formations en milieu de travail seront dispensés par des EED, etc. Elle m'a répondu que le MIFl travaille toujours à un établir un cadre pour les résidents temporaires souhaitant se prévaloir de ce programme et qu’elle nous informera lorsque ce sera défini. En ce sens, je n’ai pas de réponse définitive à te fournir pour le moment. Bien que les formations linguistiques ne constituent généralement pas des cours d'intérêt général ou d’autoperfectionnement, nous allons devoir nous pencher plus avant sur le type de formation offert en milieu de travail afin de déterminer si un permis d’études est requis ou non. Je te tiendrai au courant des développements de ce dossier. Merci et bonne journée, Melanie Bergeron

Bonjour Amélie, Merci bcp de ce retour. Aussi, j'aimerais valider avec toi mon interprétation de la réponse car celle-ci aura des répercussions importantes pour un nombre considérable de résidents temporaires au Québec. Les résidents temporaires au Québec qui souhaitent bénéficier du programme de francisation du MIFl (cours de français) à temps plein pour une période de plus de 6 mois doivent obtenir un permis d’études et ce, nonobstant le fait qu'ils étudient dans un Établissement d'enseignement désigné (EED) ou non. Cela aura un impact important pour notamment (mais pas exclusivement) les détenteurs de PT-O qui sont maintenant admissibles au programme de francisation du Québec.

## Merci de valider ce qui précède ou de m’aider dans l’interprétation de la réponse ci-dessous.

### Objet : RE: Francisation au Québec et PT-0 R205(c)(ii) (C42)--IM-2019-1731--due 25-Dec-19

#### Bonjour Amélie,

Merci de la réponse. Comme il y a beaucoup de préoccupation sur le terrain, j’aurais besoin de quelques clarifications.

2A-2019-16114-000395

mmigration, Refugees Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Question 1 : est-ce que la francisation est considérée comme de l’auto perfectionnement? Dans l’affirmative, un RT sous R205(c)(ii) pourrait étudier au-delà de 6 mois et ce, même dans un EED car l’auto-perfectionnement n’est pas considéré comme des études. Merci de me dire si cet interprétation est juste. Contexte Le gouvernement du Québec a bonifié son programme de francisation de sorte à ce que les RT puissent « se franciser » même s’ils sont détenteurs d’un permis de travail. Un volume important de détenteurs du PT-O sous R205(c)(ii) étudient présentement le français à temps plein pendant plus de 6 mois dans des EED et dans des EE non désignés. Si la « francisation » n’est pas considéré comme des études, alors les détenteurs d’un PT-O ne seront pas en bris de conditions et pourront continuer à étudier le français à temps plein avec le statut de travailleurs temporaire. Considérations Au niveau des programmes d’IRCC, la situation décrite ci-dessous semble être contradictoire car d’une part elle donne aux époux et conjoints de faits des étudiants internationaux (détenteur d’un permis d’études) et des travailleurs étrangers (détenteur d’un PT sous la catégorie NCP 0, A ou B) l’autorisation de travailler – en raison du maintien de la compétitivité du Canada. De l’autre côté, elle leur donne le droit d’étudier à temps plein sans permis d’études pendant plus de 6 mois dans EED ou EE non désignés. La situation sème également le doute et la confusion chez nos partenaires du Québec. Merci beaucoup de nous aider à clarifier cette situation. Un très beau temps des Fêtes à toi aussi! Mylene Goulet

# IPG mailbox : please close the tasking.

### Bonjour Mylène,

Question : Est-ce que les détenteurs de permis de travail ouverts sous R205 (c) (ii) pourraient se retrouver en bris de condition dans ce cas de figure? Naturellement, la question ne se pose pas pour ceux qui étudient dans un programme de moins de 6 mois ou dans tout autre établissement non-désigné. Réponse: Effectivement, si la personne qui a un permis de travail ouvert sous R205(c)(ii) étudie pour plus de 6 mois, elle se retrouverait en bris de conditions. La personne devrait obtenir un permis d’études si elle compte étudier pour une période de plus de 6 mois. J’espère que ça répond. Joyeuses fêtes! Amélie Laporte-Lestage

on health and social services -- IM-2020-0183 -- DUE February 25, 2020

IPG FG mailbox, please close this file.

Bryce, please note the subject FG request and my response in the tracking document.

Thanks very much,

## Louise

Question:

We are seeking program guidance in relation to the Temporary Public Policy (TPP) regarding excessive demand on health or social services (M05) under A38(1)©.

Based on my research, I have discovered a possible source of some miscommunication in regards to the implementation of the TPP and whether or not the application of the exemption/decision is on Humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) grounds. As per the PDI for the TPP;

Once an IME is completed, officers delegated to overcome an excessive demand inadmissibility finding, through the consideration and application of the public policy and under the authority of section A25.2, may grant an exemption from paragraph A38(1)(c) (medical inadmissibility due to excessive demand on health services and

## on social services) to the foreign national (principal applicant or their accompanying or non-accompanying

### dependent family members) who meets the criteria and conditions of the public policy.

However, under the section for processing instruction for the cases that meet the TPP, it states;

If a likely danger to public health or public safety does not exist, the officer should record an application note advising that excessive demand has been addressed by application of the public policy provisions and do all of the following:

update the medical admissibility status activity for the excessive demand individual from “Ready to be Assessed” to “Passed” (Emphasis added)

It was recently suggested that the visa officer could simply make the change to the medical status from “ready to be assessed” to “passed” if the applicant meets the TPP and has no other medical concerns. However, based on above, it appears that while we are simply passing the meds, we are in fact making an H&C decision under A25.2 of the act and would therefore require the delegated authority to make such a decision as part of the

## action of changing the meds from “ready to be assessed” to “passed”.

I seek clarification in regards to whether the implementation of the TPP to change medical status from "ready to be assessed" to "passed" is in fact an H&C decision under A25.2 of the act.

Response:

2A-2019-16114-000404

Hi Anthony,

Please note that the temporary public policy on excessive demand on health and social services is authorized under section 25.2 of the IRPA (i.e., the public policy provision); it is not an assessment under s 25 (i.e., humanitarian and compassionate considerations).

The delegations for public policies under A25.2 of the IRPA are outlined in Item 75 of the Instrument of Designation and Delegation Instrument of Designation and Delegation (PDF, 838 KB)

#### Item 75 reads as follows:

# A25.2(1)

Delegation – Where a foreign national is inadmissible or does not meet the requirements of this

## Act, grant permanent resident status or an exemption from any applicable criteria or obligations of

## the Act if it is authorized by an existing public policy established by the Minister.

Where a foreign national is inadmissible or does not meet the requirements of this Act, refuse to

# grant permanent resident status or an exemption from any applicable criteria or obligation of the

Act if the foreign national does not meet the criteria of the existing public policy issued by the Minister.

examination only.

## Subject:RE: Home Child-Care Provider Pilot and Home Support Worker Pilot: -- IM-2020-0111

-- DUE 11-Feb-20

Hi Scott, The intent of the Home Child Care Provider and Home Support Worker Pilots is to meet the needs of private individuals and families requiring full-time care in their own home. Group home settings, including retirement/senior homes, as well as daycares, do not qualify under these pilots; the place of work must be a private residence. This applies even if the caregiver resides with multiple clients requiring care. The pilots align with the description in the National Occupational Classification (NOC) codes 4411 and 4412. Work performed in healthcare service provider facilities and retirement homes would more closely align with other NOCs and as such do not qualify under this pilot. For example: o NOC 4214 Early childhood educators and assistants: "They are employed in child-care centres, daycare centres, kindergartens, agencies for exceptional children and other settings where early childhood

## education services are provided."

oNOC 3413 Nurse aides, orderlies and patient service associates. # Subject:RE: ICD Question: C20 Reciprocal Employment--IM-2020-0002-due 16-Jan-20

IPG mailbox-please close the tasking.

### Hi Stefanie,

### Thank you for your patience!

When assessing a C20 applications officers are required to assess whether or not the entry to the labour market would be neutral in the sense that Canadians have similar opportunities abroad through the reciprocity demonstrated by the employer.

Note that there is no experience requirement for C20, however, being currently employed with the company is a key feature for companies to be allowed to use C20. Commencing employment with the company upon arrival in Canada would not provide the foreign national or Canadian employee the opportunity of being able to benefit from an exchange of knowledge or experience.

If the employee is not already working for the organization abroad, it would be difficult to determine how they could take part in the organization's global exchange program. In order for reciprocity to exist, an employer/employee relationship must be created in advance of the consideration for the LMIA exemption.

In addition, it is not necessary that there be exact reciprocity (i.e. one for one exchange), but the general order of magnitude of exchanges should be reasonably similar on an annual basis. In assessing reciprocity, one would consider the relative number and percentage. For example, for exchanges involving larger numbers of foreign nationals (e.g. greater than 25), officers could require a higher minimum proportion of Canadians employed abroad to foreign nationals employed in Canada (e.g. at least 75%) than for smaller exchanges.

However, there are also cases that can allow for indirect reciprocity such as:

Reciprocity in case of multinational corporations (Deloitte, Google, Amazon, etc.)

In the case of multinational corporations (i.e. Deloitte, KPMG, etc.) there could be situations where the exchange could involve multiple countries where a Canadian goes to Deloitte in country X, but a worker from Deloitte in country Y comes to Canada as part of the exchange. This type of “indirect reciprocity" should be well documented as part of the company's global mobility plan.

Organizations that arrange volunteer or work placements

Reciprocity may be enabled and demonstrated by an organization that arranges volunteer/work placements for foreign nationals with Canadian host organizations, and where Canadians have similar opportunities, through that organization, with host organizations abroad. While the employer would be the Canadian host organization, evidence of reciprocity from the organization arranging the volunteer/work placement would have to be included in the work permit application. Reciprocity may also be demonstrated by way of a program, arrangement, or other agreement, so long as it is clear to officers that Canadians receive similar opportunities abroad.

2A-2019-16114-000410

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

For example, in the case of an organization such as MITACS/Global link that coordinates work placements for several employers, and is therefore the one that needs to demonstrate reciprocity, they would normally have a 'chapter' or an affiliate in another country where the workers would come from.

Organizations that are not affiliated or related but have signed an MoU/agreement

In addition, organizations that are not affiliated or related but have signed an MoU or some kind of agreement that supports worker exchanges and the parties have been able to demonstrate reciprocity could be considered under the C20 exemption – this would be more common between academic/public/not-for-profit institutions or between research

# institutes and private companies, but probably less likely between two corporations due to intellectual property,

competition, R&D protocols and related considerations.

### I hope this is helpful.

# Thanks,

Good morning IPG,

ICD has received a reconsideration request regarding a client who submitted two WP applications within the last six months under exemption code C20 (Canadian Interest – Reciprocal Employment). Both applications were refused with

## the following reasons:

- You have not demonstrated that you come within the exceptions under section 186 of the IRPR exempting you from the requirement to obtain a work permit or that your employment in Canada comes within the exceptions to section 203 of the IRPR. As a result, your offer of employment must be the subject of an economic effect determination before a work permit can be issued to you. Your employer in Canada should contact the local office of the Department of Employment and Social Development Canada to begin this process.
- I am not satisfied that you have proven that a reciprocal exchange exists between your employer... and the company in Canada. The PDI's say that applicants under C20 must “demonstrate that reciprocity exists", and that it should result in “a neutral labour market impact”. They don't seem to specify whether or not the applicant must already be working for the receiving company. Would you be able to clarify if officers should be assessing whether or not there is a reciprocal exchange between applicant's current and prospective employers as well as whether there is “a neutral labour market impact"? Thank you in advance,

Thank you for your feedback and the table, this is very helpful.

Taking another look at the provision under R200(3)(e) and wanted to clarify my point and explain why I think there may be an error in the online interpretation-if we focus on the first sentence of the provision (green below), which states that if you violate α condition you will be ineligible and the 6 month ban applies-this seems to apply to a FN that is in violation of one or more conditions of a previous work permit-not restricted to foreign nationals that are in violation of just one condition.

While the letter "a" can mean a restriction to only "one" in different contexts, in the legal context of 200(3)(e) seems to be unrestricted. It seems unusual for the regulations not to specify that only one condition is acceptable as this single fact is so important in this area.

Then, the provision goes on to state which conditions do not apply to the ban, described under 185(a), any of subparagraphs under 185(b)(i) to (iii) or 185(c) - again there is no restriction to the number of conditions and it actually seems to confirm for us that there are a number of conditions that could be violated. Furthermore, reading and interpreting this regulation as a whole, the provisions seem to be telling us this in simple words: "section 200(3)(e) is to be ignored unless the following applies: (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) - and this seems to further support that the letter "a" in

### R200(3)(e) does not restrict the number of violations under (ii).

Here is another scenario that seems to support this view... Let's say that the foreign national stopped working without authorization more than six months ago, provision (i) applies and we look no further even though he could have been in violation of more than one condition.

Hi Silvia,

Hopefully you had a good weekend. This is in response to your question about the online guidance regarding the 6- month ban.

Regarding your comment on POEs, please note that restoration of status cannot be granted at the POE. Individuals who have failed to comply with the conditions imposed under section R185 need to apply in Canada for restoration of their status. If they leave Canada, they will be deemed to be seeking a new entry on their return.

# Unauthorized work or study

There are several factors that could be applied under paragraph R200(3)(e). Only 1 of the following factors [R200(3)(e)(i) to (iv)] needs to apply for the officer to refuse the work permit.

(i) Unauthorized work or study and 6 months not elapsed As per subparagraph R200(3)(e)(i), the officer should not issue a work permit if either of the following applies:
- the foreign national worked or studied in Canada even though they never held a previous work or study permit, nor were they authorized to work [R196]
- the foreign national worked or studied in Canada under authorization but did not comply with the imposed conditions [R200(3)(e)(ii)]
The officer may however issue a work permit as long as 6 months have passed since the foreign national stopped their unauthorized work or study.

Note: Under subsection R182(1), officers may reinstate or restore the status of temporary

residents who have failed to comply with subparagraphs R185(b)(i) to (iii) only if they have met the following restrictions:

- they have not been out of status for more than 90 days
- they have not otherwise failed to comply with the specified conditions of their stay
- At POEs:
(ii) Failed to comply with more than 1 imposed condition – we cannot make a connection to the regs as to the 1 only condition.

As per subparagraph R200(3)(e)(ii), seems a few words are missing here; should this be added: a work permit or study permit shall not be issued if the foreign national has failed to comply with a condition of a previous permit or authorization, unless the study or work was unauthorized only because the foreign national did not comply with conditions imposed under paragraph R185(a), subparagraphs R185(b)(i) to (iii) or paragraph R185(c). Paragraphs R185(d) and (e) are not included in these exemptions.

If the foreign national did not comply with only 1 imposed condition, a work permit can be issued as long as they have applied for restoration of their temporary resident status.

nmigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canada et Citoyenneté Canada cion disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l'accès à l’informatior However, if the foreign national did not comply with more than 1 imposed condition, they may not be issued a work permit under paragraph R200(3)(e). we cannot make a connection to the regs as to the more than 1 imposed condition. The regs seem to suggest that there can be multiple instances of non-compliance as long as they fall within the prescribed subsections and paragraphs in R185. See Conditions and validity period on work permits for more details.

# Example

A temporary worker was authorized to work for employer A as a waiter until July 15, 2017, and continued working beyond July 15 without applying for a new work permit. Please clarify what the violations are in this example... to me the violation is R185(a), but others are of the opinion that the violation here is R185(b)(iv).

If the foreign national otherwise meets eligibility and admissibility requirements, they could be issued a new work permit without waiting for 6 months to elapse. However, if the temporary worker was authorized to work for employer A as a waiter until July 15, 2017, and on August 15, 2017, they began working for employer B as a waiter, their work is considered “unauthorized” and they must wait for 6 months to pass since the day the work for employer A stopped before a work permit can be issued. We were unable to link this statement to the regs... my understanding is that if you were in non compliance for working for a different employer and work permit expired, that would be 185(a) and 185(b)(ii) which are both acceptable types of non compliance and the 6 month ban should not apply.

Sent: March 11, 2020 11:38 AM To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC); Program Integrity / Integrité des Programmes (IRCC) Cc: DN Risk Assessment / Évaluation des Risques RN (IRCC); Raimondo.Angelo Subject: RE: MANIL2020-102-Putting an IRPA admissibility lens on the criminality and security situation in the Philippines -- IM-2020-0222 -- DUE March 4, 2020

Thank you for your question. The word "offence" implies that it be of a criminal nature. As such, for sections 36(1)(c) or 36(2)(c) to be applied, there has to be a criminal offence in the country the offence was committed. Therefore, a matter decided in civil court cannot be used for the purposes of determining inadmissibility pursuant to 36(1)(c) or 36(2)(c).

#### We trust this is of assistance.

Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Question:

The Centralized Network would like clarification regarding triage for all Permanent Resident applications where an applicant is deemed M5. Specifically, limited guidance currently exists in relations to the application of the Temporary Public Policy for Excessive Demand on Health and Social Services.

Currently, the DN APR File Dispatch Rules indicate that all M05 cases should be transferred to HM-NF. We have been informed that in practice this pertains only to cases where the public policy may not apply, however the PDl on excessive demand states that:

All applications with 1 or more excessive demand medical assessments in the Domestic Network and Centralized Network were centralized at the HMID-NF before June 1, 2018.

Additionally, there is a discrepancy with current internal triage for criteria for LOBs such as FSW and PNP as these indicate explicitly that if "one or more clients on file have received an M05 medical assessment and are eligible for the public policy exemption" that the application should be processed by the appropriate CN office.

Could IPG please advise whether M5 TPP should be triaged to the appropriate DN office for processing or if these remains the responsibility of the processing office? We would appreciate clarification regarding all PR lines of business, including those such as CEC where triage criteria do not exist.

Answer:

Centralized Network (CN) should use the same triage criteria (as it relates to M5s) for CEC and FST that is posted here: federal skilled worker class (FSWC) electronic applications submitted after January 1, 2015. PNP e-APRs has the same triage criteria for M5s as FSW.

Triage criteria to the Centralized Network (CN)

Foreign skilled worker e-APRs that meet the following criteria are likely to be less complex and should be triaged for processing in Canada by the appropriate CN office, according to the dispatch rules for the CN:

one or more clients on file have received an M05 medical assessment and are eligible for the public policy exemption

Triage criteria to the Domestic Network (DN)

Foreign skilled worker e-APRs that meet the following criteria should be triaged for processing in Canada to the appropriate DN office, according to the dispatch rules for the DN*:

one or more clients on file have received an M05 medical assessment and are not eligible for the public policy exemption

As CN is required to determine whether the applicant is eligible for the public policy exemption prior to applying the triage criteria, an delegated decision (check the IL3) maker at CN would have to do an analysis first.

*All M5s where the TPP does not apply should be triaged to the Humanitarian Migration and Integrity Division at the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) Niagara Falls office (HMID-NF). This should be added to CNs dispatch rules.

CN must ensure that all possible decisions are made on the application before transferring it to HMID-NF, i.e., eligibility, criminality, etc.

We trust that this information will assist you.

The Centralized Network would like clarification regarding triage for all Permanent Resident applications where an applicant is deemed M5. Specifically, limited guidance currently exists in relations to the application of the Temporary Public Policy for Excessive Demand on Health and Social Services.

Currently, the DN APR File Dispatch Rules indicate that all M05 cases should be transferred to HM-NF. We have been informed that in practice this pertains only to cases where the public policy may not apply, however thePD on excessive demand states that:

Bonjour Liliane, Nous ne sommes pas au courant qu'une lettre d’ERAR positif ait eu une telle mention, mais nous vérifierons avec les bureaux qui traitent les demandes ERAR et ferons un rappel si nécessaire. Tel que tu le mentionnes, nos lettres ne comportent pas une mention de ce genre. Le texte qui se trouve actuellement sur nos lettres se veut de nature plus générale et ne confirme pas un type particulier de couverture, mais souligne plutôt au demandeur que la couverture peut avoir changé, tout dépendamment de ce qu'elle était avant. Nous avons pris note de la suggestion d'envoyer un avis, mais dans le contexte de l’ERAR, il y a plusieurs étapes entre la décision et le moment où cette décision est remise au demandeur par l’ASFC, il serait plus difficile de faire en sorte que l'avis soit remis de façon consistante. Ainsi, nous

## allons conserver notre manière actuelle d’informer les demandeurs, mais nous nous assurerons que l’information soit

claire. Note cependant que nous sommes en processus de mettre à jour toutes les lettres et que le délai de 45 jours qui est mentionné dans les spécimens qui t'avaient été envoyés doit être corrigé pour 90 jours. Cordialement, Mireille

Bonjour Raoul,

Veuillez trouver ici-bas la réponse à votre question :

Q: Following the received instructions regarding pending security results, is it possible to please clarify where (or how) to see if a communication request (Comms Request) has been sent by NSSD to the Mission & also, if the required information was provided to them.

A: IRCC Migration Unit oversea would receive Comms Requests from the NSSD through a pre-determined IRCC generic email address or to a specified person or both. The Comms Request is then actioned by the appropriate unit (TR/PR) or to another unit who's responsible to contact applicants to obtain the requested information; The unit responsible then (should) enters the Comms Request in GCMS notes. (ex: Comms request received this day from the NSSD) The information required from the Comms Request is then sent to the applicant either by email (Not the Comms request itself from NSSD-but the info requested) or by phone in order to acquire the missing information. When information is obtained, an email reply is sent to the NSSD original requester with the sought information, and at that point, IRCC (LES or CBOs) should make an annotation in GCMS notes that information it has been sent back to NSSD. (as per normal procedures when an activity/action is taken in an application)

suggested in order to establish if this is the case.

could be used for future verifications' exercise.

We hope this answers your question and remain available for further support if required.

Regards,

Benoit

Nous avons reçu une réponse à une demande d'orientation fonctionnelle. Celle-ci était au sujet des demandes de résidence permanente en traitement mais qui sont depuis un bon moment en attente pour l'obtention des résultats sécuritaires

Or, suite à la réponse reçue pouvez-vous svp prendre les actions suivantes :

1. Veuillez svp identifier les demandes en traitement qui se trouvent dans votre charge de travail et donc vous êtes toujours en attente des résultats au niveau sécuritaire.
2. En révisant les notes au SMGC, vérifier si la Division du filtrage pour la sécurité nationale (DFSN), a fait parvenir une demande aux fins de communications à la Mission à l’étranger.
3. Si la demande aux fins de communications a été effectuée, est-ce qu'on a obtenu les informations ou une réponse?
4. Si l'information n’a toujours pas été obtenue ou si la DFSN n'a pas fait parvenir de demande aux fins de communications, svp effectuer cette demande.
5. Si toutes ces étapes ont déjà été complétées et que tout semble être en ordre, svp faire parvenir un courriel à l’adresse générique de la Division du filtrage pour la sécurité nationale (DFSN) à CBSA-ASFC_NSSD-DFSN NSSD-DFSN@cbsa-asfc.gc.ca Svp inclure les informations suivantes dans le courriel : (STS) CA# ainsi que le UCl# Veuillez demander une mise-à-jour sur la requête au niveau sécuritaire en spécifiant que la requête est « en attente » depuis le (svp indiquer la date depuis quand). Demander si des informations supplémentaires sont requises de la part de la Mission à l’étranger afin de compléter le processus sécuritaire
Il est important de ne pas soumettre à nouveau la demande pour l'obtention de résultats sécuritaires mais de plutôt suivre les étapes décrites dans ce courriel Nous avons plusieurs demandes qui sont dans cette situation, dans nos lignes d’affaires. Veuillez svp prendre action pour les demandes qui vous sont assignées

Si vous avez des questions, svp m’en faire part

Merci

# Hello,

With respects toquestion 2'Officers would like more guidance on OB 666. If a security result is pending for a permanent resident application, does an officer wait for the result, re-visit or resend?'

Officers should not resend the security referral. Usually, security screening with a "Pending" status are explained by the fact that a request for more information was sent from NSSD to the Mission regarding the applicant (i.e: Missing employment information, Military table not filled properly, etc...) and the Mission has not provided the required information back, or, NSSD has received the information from the Mission but either an analyst has not reviewed the case yet (especially in the case of permanent resident applicants which take longer to review than temporary resident applicants) or in rare cases, the analyst forgot to switch the status from "Pending" after examination.

In order to establish at what stage the screening review is at, Migration officers should:

- Review the case notes and establish if a communication request (Comms Request) has been sent by NSSD to the Mission and if so, if the required information was provided to them. If information was not provided, complete the comms request. If all seems to be in order, Mission is to:
- Send an email to the NSSD generic mailbox address at: CBSA-ASFC_NSSD-DFSN NSSD-DFSN@cbsa-asfc.gc.ca; Email should include:
(STS) CA# and UCI# and request an update on the screening by stating that the status is currently "Pending" since (insert date) and enquire if more information is required from the Mission in order to complete the screening process.

NSSD answer to these requests relatively quickly.

HI,

I work with Migration Health Branch policy and I would appreciate a bit of information in how processing takes place at POEs (e.g. Vancouver Int'I Airport, Pearson Int'I Airport, etc.). I have bolded my questions for faster view.

I note the following instructions to officers at the POE concerning clients with the PG-1 visa as outline in OB357:

#### Port of Entry (POE)

consider the applicant to have fulfilled the eligibility criteria for a Super Visa upon presentation of a PG-1 single or multiple-entry counterfoil, or letter of introduction from a visa office abroad, unless new or different information that is pertinent to this decision has become known subsequent to the issuance of that counterfoil or letter of introduction; and normally fix the period of authorized stay as two years pursuant to the provisions of S.183 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) and stamp the applicant's passport or travel document for a duration of two years; or issue a visitor record in the case of an applicant who is not required to be in possession of a passport, pursuant to S.52(2) of IRPR.

For further clarity, examining officers at a POE should refer to the Canada Border Services Agency OB.

## FOSS Special Program Code: PG1

## A few quick questions:

1. When a client first presents themselves at a POE with a multi-entry PG-1 visa (or letter from introduction from a visa office), is the client's passport stamped at primary or secondary or is this discretionary and determined at primary? The client's passport is stamped at primary.
a. At primary of secondary normally is there any other action taken besides stamping the passport for a stay valid for a maximum of two years (assuming there is no concern with the length of stay for the PG-1 visa)? No other actions assuming there are no other concerns or documents to issue.
2. When a client then represents themselves at a POE with a multi-entry PG-1 visa having already been to Canada previously, do they receive the repeat stamp on their passport at primary or are they treated again as if it is a 'first entry'? Every time a foreign national presents themselves at a POE it is considered a new entry (we don't really speak in terms of first or second entry) however if the PG1 holder is returning from a weekend of shopping in the U.S. they may be readmitted on their previous stamp. That is at the discretion of the BSO.
a. In either of the above two situations, does the POE look up the client to determine if they require an IMM035 (medical surveillance undertaking form) and forward a completed IMM1035 to the Public Health Liaison Unit at Migration Health Branch? This is not part of CBSA's PG1 procedures and given the time constraints at the POE it is highly unlikely that this would happen.
The reason I am asking is because my understanding is that usually the IMM0535 is generated for PR clients (if requiring a medical surveillance undertaking form), or to workers/students who have been identified as requiring the IMM035 form and this is done at secondary. Most standard TR visitor visas for under 6 months are handled at primary and would not normally have an IMM0535 issued (for obvious logistic reasons). Is the PG-1 visa handled in a manner similar to the more standard 6 month visitor visa? I would say that PG1 holders are handled similar to regular visitors.

BTW: Hard to believe 2020 is already here. Wishing you all a happy new year!

Importance:High

##### Hello Erika,

Thank you for contacting us with your question.

You are correct to wonder if one representative can represent a group of people. One representative can represent any number of applicants, but each applicant must complete and submit a Use of a representative form (IMM 5476) for their application (or matter). Furthermore, if one applicant is using the representative to assist with more than one application (or matter), the same applicant must complete and sign a separate IMM 5476 for each application (or matter).

Said another way, each application (or matter) requires its own Use of a representative form even if the applicant and the representative are the same people on different applications. Also, in the case of a PR application where there are often more than one applicant, each applicant 18 years of age and over on that application must complete and submit their own Use of a representative form for that application.

Thus, to answer your question, no, the lawyer cannot present one IMM 5475/5476 for a whole community of people.

For your information, I am referencing a webpage below. It is from the IMM 5476 Use of a representative form guide. It might be helpful for you in supporting your position to the representative in question. I have cut and pasted the first paragraphs of the guide.

[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-) guides/guide-5561-instructions-use-representative.html

# Guide 5561 - Instructions-Use of a Representative

## Completing the form

##### Use of a Representative (IMM 5476)

##### Who may use this form?

##### Complete this form only if you:

2A-2019-16114-000468

and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l'accès à l’information

- are appointing a representative;
- have to update contact information for your previously appointed representative; or
- are cancelling a representative's appointment.
If you have dependent children aged 18 years or older, they are required to complete their own copy of this form if a representative is also conducting business on their behalf.

## Who is a representative?

A representative is someone who provides advice, consultation, or guidance to you at any stage of the application process, or in a proceeding and, if you appoint them as your representative by filling out this form, has your permission to conduct business on your behalf with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

You are not obliged to hire a representative. We treat everyone equally, whether they use the service of a representative or not.

## When you appoint a representative:

- you also authorize IRCC and CBSA to share information from your case file with this person in place of you. Please note the representative will receive all correspondence from IRCC or the CBSA, not the applicant; your application will not be given special attention nor can you expect faster processing or a more favourable outcome; the representative is authorized to represent you only on citizenship or immigration matters related to the application you submit with this form; and
- you can appoint only one (1) representative for each application you submit.
1 Important information: You must notify IRCC if your representative's contact information changes, or if you change your representative, or cancel the appointment of your representative. For more information on updating IRCC with your representative's information, please see below section-Notify IRCC about any changes.

The general Use of representatives web information for the public is found at: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-) guides/use-representative.html

Let us know if you have further questions.

### Good day.

As you may well be aware of, there are times when a nominating province may place their nomination on hold pending an investigation. When this occurs on a file that is already in progress at IRCC, the associated application will be placed on hold until such a time as the province confirms whether they intend to rescind the nomination or to continue supporting it. When it comes to investigations, there is no standard time frame identified. Rescinded nominations result in the associated application being refused as the client no longer meets the requirements of R87(2)(a). When the province reviews and determines they have no concerns and wishes to continue supporting the nomination, the associated application will be placed back into processing queues and reviewed accordingly.

Unfortunately there are times (some recently) where there is a break down in communication that occurs after a file has been placed on hold.

When CN officers come across these situations, they send correspondence to the key contact for that province asking for confirmation whether the file remains on hold or if it can re-enter the processing queue. A note is to be then entered into the application. Current bilateral agreements with the provinces and territories are that the province or territory is to respond within 60 to 90 days, depending on the province or territory. Recently, we have experienced that a number of key contacts are not responding to these requests within the timeframe set out in the provincial agreements, and others, at times not at all. This unfortunately affects our ability to effectively manage our inventories, it is negative client service, is not in the spirit of the program and does not foster strong working relationships between the federal and provincial governments.

Would IPG and/or IRM be able to assist us in working with the provinces and territories to ensure that responses to IRCC requests for information, including but not limited to investigations, are received within a reasonable time? If we should be asking for this information in a different manner than we have in the past, please advise as to how we should proceed in the future (for example, should we be sending a request to the program integrity box for IRM to follow up

## with the province? Should we go through CMB?).

Thank you in advance for any assistance and guidance.

Shannon Morrissey Citizenship & Immigration Case Processing Officer, Centralized Network Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada / Government of Canada Shannon.Morrissey@cic.gc.ca

Good day,

### Thank you for your question.

Similar to the Passport Act, IRPA allows the Minister to use an electronic system/automated system to make decisions or determinations under the Act. In GCMS, it is recorded in a way that the system (GCMS) makes an "approved" decision as an officer on behalf of the Minister. As it stands, GCMS-system is listed as an employee in GCMS; therefore, any decisions or determinations made by the GCMS-system is recorded as a decision/determination that is made by the GCMS-system.

### I hope this is helpful.

Best regards,

I'm sure you have a lot on your place right now so this is really not urgent-just a response to a FG for you review and approval :

- Dès que la décision ERAR est reçue, la personne pourra donc immédiatement déposer une demande CH?
S'il s’agit d'un étranger désigné, celui-ci ne peut demander l’étude de son cas CH que si cinq années se sont écoulées depuis l'un ou l’autre des jours suivants :

L25(1)(1.01)(a) : Il a fait une demande d'asile sans avoir fait une demande de protection, le jour où il a été statué en dernier ressort sur la demande d’asile

L25(1)(1.01)(b) :S'il a fait une demande de protection, le jour où il a été statué en dernier ressort sur cette demande.

Dans d'autres cas, le jour où il devient un étranger désigné.

Définition d'un étranger désigné selon L20.1(2) : Lorsqu'une désignation est faite en vertu du paragraphe (1), l'étranger — non visé à l’article 19 — qui fait partie du groupe dont l’arrivée fait l'objet de la désignation devient un étranger désigné sauf si, à son arrivée, il détient les visas ou autres documents réglementaires et que, à la suite d’un contrôle, l’agent est convaincu qu'il n’est pas interdit de territoire. Il s’agit donc de toutes les arrivées irrégulières ou impliquant l'organisation de l'entrée illégale de personnes.

S'il ne s’agit pas d’un étranger désigné, celui-ci pourra déposer une demande CH dès que la décision sur sa demande ERAR sera rendue.

Une personne dont la demande d’asile est irrecevable pourra déposer sa demande CH avant sa demande ERAR – dans ce cas, est-ce que sa demande CH sera suspendue pendant l’étude de sa demande ERAR?

Non, si celui-ci dépose sa demande CH avant sa demande ERAR, les deux applications seront traitées en même temps.

# Merci, Mireille Sebahana

# Bonjour,

2A-2019-16114-000485


<!-- CHUNK_BOUNDARY 2A-2019-16114_part2_00160.md -->

mmigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Lors de la dernière rencontre du Comité consultatif sur la qualité des services d’IRCC et de l’ASFC en décembre dernier, il a été question du nouveau sous-alinéa ajouté à L25 : (1.2) Le ministre ne peut étudier la demande de l’étranger faite au titre du paragraphe (1) dans les cas suivants :

· b.1) sa demande d’asile a fait l’objet d’un constat d’irrecevabilité et sa demande de protection au ministre est toujours pendante;

Les instructions au sujet de la réception et l’admissibilité pour les demandes CH ont été abordés avec les partenaires, celles-ci indiquant qu’il est interdit à une personne de demander des CH si elle a présenté une demande d’asile dont on a déterminé qu’elle est inadmissible à être transmise à la SPR, et la personne a une demande d’ERAR qui est en instance.

Les partenaires ont posé les questions suivantes :

- Dès que la décision ERAR est reçue, la personne pourra donc immédiatement déposer une demande CH? Une personne dont la demande d’asile est irrecevable pourra déposer sa demande CH avant sa demande ERAR – dans ce cas, est-ce que sa demande CH sera suspendue pendant l’étude de sa demande ERAR?
Nous avons indiqué aux partenaires que l’article L25(1.2) est libellé 'le Ministre ne peut étudier la demande...', ce qui laisse croire que la demande CH ne ferait pas l’objet d’un examen pendant l’étude de la demande ERAR dans un tel scénario.

Pourriez-vous fournir des réponses aux questions à partager avec les partenaires? À noter que la prochaine rencontre est prévue pour le 25 mars 2020.

À titre informatif, le Comité consultatif sur la qualité des services se réunit à chaque trimestre à Montréal. En plus d’IRCC et de l’ASFC, les membres sont composés de représentants d’ONGs offrant des services aux personnes immigrantes et réfugiés, de représentants d’associations d’avocats et de consultants en immigration, PRAIDA (organisme sous le ministère de la santé du Québec offrant des services aux demandeurs d’asile), HCR, Aide juridique, MIFI.

# Merci beaucoup,

Bonjour Liliane,

### Désolée pour le délai.

Voici les réponses à tes questions spécifiques :

La division en charge des demandes ERAR (Migration humanitaire et Intégrité) travaille à mettre en œuvre les procédures ainsi que tous les aspects techniques relatifs aux audiences obligatoires. Pour le moment, les agents responsables sont en Ontario et les audiences se dérouleront par vidéoconférence. Une évaluation des procédures sera faite et des modifications pourraient être apportées.

Les partenaires ont posé les questions suivantes : Dans le cas des détenus, quelles seront les procédures? Les audiences par vidéoconférence auront-elles lieu dans les mêmes salles que les autres clients?

2A-2019-16114-000487

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act Lnfomn

Les procédures seront adaptées selon les circonstances de chaque cas, puisque la réalité de chaque centre de détention est différente. Cependant, nous pouvons confirmer que si possible, les audiences seront organisées par vidéoconférence, soit à partir du centre de détention, soit à partir d'un bureau d'IRCC ou de l'ASFC. Les procédures pour chaque audience sont établies avec un souci d’équité procédurale.

Les salles d'audiences où les demandeurs sont vus par vidéoconférence varieront selon l'endroit où l'audience aura lieu. Si l'audience a lieu dans les bureaux d'IRCC, il s’agit des mêmes salles.

Dans les cas où le client n’est pas accompagné à l’audience par un représentant/conseiller, serait-il possible qu’il le soit par un bénévole? Comme l’audience n’est pas enregistrée, cette personne pourrait prendre des notes et représenter aussi une présence rassurante pour le client.

Si un demandeur veut être accompagné à l'audience, il doit remplir un formulaire IMM 5476 et désigner cette personne comme représentant non-rémunéré.

Cordialement, Mireille

## Sent: March 4, 2020 12:28 PM To:'Marc-Andre.Billette@international.gc.ca'

# Cc:IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC)

FW: Question dossier Québec -- IM-2020-0079

# Subject:

### Bonjour,

Ce courriel est en reponse a votre correspondance datee du 23 Janvier 2020, concernant Question dossier Quebec.

Question 1- Petite question concernant les dossiers temporaires pour le Québec, à savoir à quel point nous pouvons les refuser pour BF ou autre.

Voici un exemple, j'ai un dossier WP pour une aide-familiale/ Live-in Caregiver et elle a son CAQ. La famille demande une aide-familiale pour 1 enfant de 13 ans. Donc est-ce que je pourrais refuser la demande selon le fait que la famille n’a pas besoin d'une aide-familiale, mais qu'elle cherche plutôt à avoir une femme de ménage (tel que mentionné dans Connexion : Note : Les travaux ménagers, le nettoyage et les autres tâches domestiques similaires, comme la préparation des repas, peuvent représenter une petite partie de l’ensemble des fonctions décrites dans le contrat d’emploi,

### lorsqu’elles relèvent clairement du cadre des soins prodigués; toutefois, ces tâches domestiques ne peuvent

constituer la fonction principale d'un aide familial résidant éventuel.)

ou bien vu que le Québec lui a délivré son CAQ, mais je ne peux refuser la demande sous cet angle ?

Réponse 1- : Oui. Il peut si il n’est pas satisfait que le demandeur rencontre les exigences du programme. Le Québec est responsable de la sélection des immigrants mais la décision finale revient à IRCC.

8.6 Demandeurs à destination du Québec En vertu de l’article 22b) de l’Accord Canada-Québec, le Québec doit donner son consentement en vue de l’admission dans la province de tout travailleur temporaire étranger dont l’admission est assujettie aux exigences du Canada en matière de disponibilité des travailleurs canadiens. Un demandeur qui souhaite se rendre au Québec au titre du PAFR doit obtenir un CAQ avant de présenter à CIC une demande de permis de travail aux termes du PAFR. Le MICC délivre un CAQ après un examen du dossier selon ses critères de sélection. Tous les demandeurs au titre du PAFR doivent démontrer à l’agent de visas du Canada qu’ils répondent à tous critères du R112. L'agent fédéral des visas doit s'assurer que tous les critères du R112 sont respectés. Le demandeur doit répondre à tous les critères propres au PAFR indiqués au R112 ainsi qu'aux autres critères du RIPR, que le MICC délivre ou non un CAQ. Le personnel des bureaux des visas doit examiner les demandes des demandeurs à destination du Québec comme toutes les autres et dans l’ordre où elles ont été reçues. Si un demandeur obtient un CAQ, mais ne satisfait pas aux exigences du gouvernement fédéral, ce sont les dispositions réglementaires fédérales qui priment. Il faut refuser les demandes de ces demandeurs. La délivrance d’un CAQ ne garantit pas automatiquement la délivrance d’un permis de travail aux termes du PAFR.
2A-2019-16114-000491

mmigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Question 2- Aussi, la même question se pose concernant les étudiants. Pourrait-on refuser une demande SP du Québec s’il a son CAQ, si nous ne croyons pas qu'il s'agit d'un « Bona fide Student » qui quittera à la fin de son séjour ?

#### Réponse 2 :

#### Oui il peut.

En vertu de R216(1)(b) : l’agent délivre un permis d’études à l’étranger si, à l’issue d’un contrôle, les éléments suivants sont établis : ... b) il quittera le Canada à la fin de la période de séjour qui lui est applicable au titre de la section 2 de la partie 9;

Tous les étrangers qui présentent une demande de permis d’études doit être évaluée au cas par cas. Une décision défavorable rendue à l’endroit d’un étudiant non authentique ne peut être contestée devant les tribunaux que si la décision en question repose sur les renseignements liés au cas mis à la disposition de l’agent.

Si la bonne foi du demandeur fait l’objet de préoccupations ou de doutes pour l’agent, il doit les communiquer au demandeur qui aura alors l’occasion de s’expliquer.

J’espère que cette réponse vous sera utile. N’hésitez pas à envoyer toutes requêtes additionnelles à l’adresse suivante : IRCC.IPGFunctionalGuidance-OrientationFonctionnelleOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca

Cordialement,

L’équipe de projet du Programme des étudiants étrangers Orientation du programme d’immigration Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada

# Subject:FW: Question re: 120 WP exemption for researchers -- IM-2020-0069 -- DUE 3-Feb-20

Thanks Todd for your question.

Short response: Interns students participating in the MITACS Globlelink Research Internship seeking entry may be eligible for the 120 day GSS work permit exemption (if they meet all requirements including admissibility).

Background

Just wanted to provide you with background information on the reason behind adding the following guidance regarding the eligibility of undergraduate or graduate students who are coming to perform research with Canadian faculty at degree-granting institutions or their affiliated research institutions for the 120-day work permit exemption under the Global Skills Strategy. The guidance was included to reflect cases such as interns (awards recipients) coming through Mitacs to perform research for 120 days or less in a year in a degree granting institutions or their affiliated research institutes.

After GSS was implemented in 2017, Mitacs reached out to IRCC to examine their situation with respect to the Global Skilis Strategy. Specifically, we were asked if Mitacs could be designated as an “affiliated research institution" for the purposes of the new, short-duration research work permit exemption and as a designated referral partner (for the Dedicated Service Channel). The Department looked at the options and reported back to senior management. As an outcome of the discussion, IRCC assessed that MITACS cannot be considered as an affiliated research institute nor a degree-granting institution. Since Mitacs plays an essential role in bringing interns researchers/award recipients to Canada (hundreds of award recipients/every year), it was decided to update the GSS PDIs to include the guidance highlighted below.

While most foreign nationals coming to Canada to perform research are likely to be professionals, there may be situations where undergraduate or graduate students are coming to perform research with Canadian faculty at degree-granting institutions or their affiliated research institutions. These students may also be considered under this exemption, subject to the criteria noted above.

- Under the Global Skills Strategy, researchers coming to perform work for 120 days or less at a publicly-funded, degree-granting institution or their affiliated research institutions are eligible for a work permit exemption. Mitacs performs the role of an independent third-party granting institute. Based on a description of their programs available on their website, they link students, interns, academics, and business together to exchange and develop ideas. They are match-makers and funders, not the conductors or location of the research itself.
- In establishing this exemption, the Department worked to ensure the eligibility criteria were clear yet flexible. For example, while the exemption was restricted to research (and not teaching or other academic activities), there is no definition of “research" contained in the Public Policy that enacted
2A-2019-16114-000495

mmigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

this exemption; stakeholders told us that research takes many forms and asked that we not be prescriptive.

### Moreover, while the Public Policy specifies that the exemption is available only to researchers

### working at publicly-funded Canadian degree-granting institutions, or their affiliated research

institutions, there is also no formal, definitive list of the institutions that are eligible for this exemption. While our program delivery instructions for this exemption do provide a list of publicly-funded colleges and universities, the list is meant to be illustrative, not definitive (and no examples of affiliated research institutes are provided).

- Ultimately, whether or not the work to be performed constitutes research, and whether or not the place of research meets the threshold of a publicly-funded degree-granting institution or affiliated research institute, is ultimately at the discretion of border services officers when assessing an individual case.
- As Mitacs program participants are all working collaboratively with Canadian degree-granting institutions, they already have an institution that could issue the letter (required in GSS PDIs) for them.

Good Afternoon,

A while back I had 2 students participating the in the MITACS Globalink Research Internship seeking entry, and requesting a work permit exemption under the Public Policy facilitating entry into Canada for short term work.

The interns are in the final year of their undergraduate degree at their home institutions and had been selected to participate in research projects under the supervision of Professors at Canadian institutions for 90 days, these positions have historically required a work permit, and were exempt from the requirement to obtain and LMiA under C44. (The organization itself is an example of an internship that would require a work permit)

2A-2019-16114-000497

mmigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l'accès à l’information

Foreign nationals registered at foreign educational institutions (i.e., not enrolled in a Canadian designated learning institution) and wishing to come to Canada to complete an internship or undertake a position in research programs are considered temporary foreign workers under the IRPR. Examples include foreign nationals funded by research organizations such as Mitacs.

[http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/unique/intern-stag-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/unique/intern-stag-eng.aspx)

The interns are the ones who appear to be gaining the benefit in the form experience and training from this arrangement more so than the Canadian Intuitions that have invited them, however they are now all seeking entry under the 120 day work permit exemption for researchers:

The original wording from the Minister on this exemption states:

Similar to economic employers, Canadian degree granting institutions and affiliated research institutions sometimes require highly specialized foreign researchers for short periods of time to produce world class research. Canadian institutions are in competition with top tier research institutions from around the world to attract foreign researchers with rare and highly specialized expertise. Enacting facilitative measures via this policy will assist Canadian institutions in the recruitment of top tier researchers and increase the number of opportunities for Canadian researchers to collaborate with top tier foreign researchers.

[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-) agreements/short-term-work.html

It is difficult to see how these students could meet the definition of "top tier researcher", however the policy as well as the manuals state that delegated officers may grant the exemption if the foreign national "has a significant role to play or value to add to the research project;" As per the manuals:

In assessing whether the foreign national has a significant role to play in or value to add to the research

# project, officers may wish to consider the following:

- The applicant demonstrates academic excellence or expertise in a field related to the particular work to be undertaken. The position reflects the experience and expertise of the applicant and the role they will play in the project.
While most foreign nationals coming to Canada to perform research are likely to be professionals,there may

# be situations where undergraduate or graduate students are coming to perform research with Canadian faculty

at degree-granting institutions or their affiliated research institutions. These students may also be considered under this exemption, subject to the criteria noted above.

[http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/researcher-chercheur-exemption-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/researcher-chercheur-exemption-eng.aspx)

Any clarification you can provide on the application of the 120 WP exemption for these interns would be appreciated.

'Dominik.Viel-Leblanc@international.gc.ca' To: Katz.Miriam; IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC); Cc: 'Greg.Chubak@international.gc.ca'; 'Christopher.Perez-Parkes@international.gc.ca' FW: Question: Express Entry -- IM-2020-0174 -- DUE February 25, 2020

# Subject:

# Good Day,

Thank you for your email correspondence to IPG.

Question:

1- When applicants create an Express Entry profile, do they expressly indicate which category they want to be considered under, or is this done automatically? 2- If you receive an invitation to apply under one category, ie: CEC-does that mean that your application will ONLY be assessed under the CEC criteria, even if you may meet the requirements for other categories? 3- If you decline an invitation to apply under the CEC, is there a chance that you could later receive an ITA for a FSW application, even if you have declared work experience in Canada? 4- When you create an Express Entry profile, does it specifically ask whether Canadian Work Experience was accumulated while holding legal TR status? I understand that this is a requirement for the CEC work experience. However, if a client had Canadian Work Experience while they were a PR, but then lost their status, would they then need to respond "no" if this is how the question is formulated?

Answer:

1- Applicants do not select which program they wish to be considered under. The Express Entry (EE) system will determine under which programs the applicant may be eligible for based on their answers. Applicants may be eligible for more than one program through EE. If that is the case, they will be invited to apply for one program based on IRCCs program hierarchy order:

1. Canadian Experience Class (CEC),
2. Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP), then
3. Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP).
### For example:

If they met the criteria for all three programs, the system would send them an invitation to apply for the CEC. If they met the criteria for CEC and FSWP, they would also get an invitation to apply under the CEC. If they met the criteria for FSWP and FSTP, they would get an invitation to apply under FSWP.

2- Even if they meet the criteria of another category, the applicant can only be assessed as a CEC applicant. 3- If the applicant's declared answers are such that the EE system recognizes that they still meet CEC, and the program hierarchy is the same, they will end up being invited under CEC again. 4- Unfortunately, the system does not ask whether they held TR status which may lead some applicants to believe they qualify when they do not. Should an officer determine that the applicant does not have TR status (which a PR would not have), they may reject that period of work experience (which may lead to a refusal).

2A-2019-16114-000500

We trust that this information will assist you.

IPG Mailbox, FYI only (this request has been closed in the records)

Bonjour,

Voici les réponses aux questions qui ont été demandées suite à la formation Audiences et exclusions.

- Peut-on utiliser les informations du CH pour le ERAR?--> Non, car ce n’est pas le même cadre d’évaluation. Toutefois, on peut le faire avec une lettre d’équité procédurale. Vérifier toutefois la particularité des cas combos ou le demandeur ne fut pas avisé du refus CH... (Svp, confirmer). Il n’est habituellement pas nécessaire d’envoyer une lettre d’équité procédurale pour se référer à l’information contenue dans un CH puisque les informations contenues dans celui-ci font partie intégrante du dossier du demandeur. Il s’agit d’une preuve intrinsèque. Toutefois, les meilleures pratiques exigent qu’une copie certifiée conforme des documents contenant l’information utilisée du dossier CH soit mise au dossier de la demande ERAR (et vice-versa) puisque le dossier doit contenir l’ensemble des documents analysés par l’agent. En cas de règle 17, tous ces documents seront envoyés à la Cour fédérale. Dans certains cas particuliers, une lettre d’équité procédurale devrait effectivement être envoyée. Par exemple, dans les cas où l’information utilisée dans le CH pourrait mener à l’exclusion du demandeur. Aussi, si des questions de crédibilité sont soulevées avec l’utilisation de cette information, l’agent doit considérer la nécessité de tenir une audience afin de laisser la possibilité au demandeur de répondre sur les préoccupations qui sont soulevées. Ceci s’applique pour tous les types de dossiers (simples ou combos).
- Nouvelle preuve apportée le jour de l’audience. Pas respecté le 5 jours requis. C’est à l’API de décider si l’adjoint doit scanner le paquet en partie ou en entier (afin qu'il prenne connaissance du contenu, en entier ou en partie). Le SIO doit aviser le client que le tout doit être envoyé à HM-Vancouver (qui l’enverra ensuite à HM-Miss). Ce n’est pas au bureau local (HM-Mtl) de poster le paquet ou de le numériser en entier et l'envoyer à l'API. Svp, confirmer. Les Instructions sur l’exécution des programmes ([http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/prra-erar/hearings-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/refugees-refugies/prra-erar/hearings-) audiences-fra.aspx) mentionnent que l’agent principal d’immigration détermine si les documents reçus à l’audience peuvent être abordés lors de l’audience ou s’il est nécessaire d’expliquer au demandeur que les documents reçus à l’audience ne peuvent pas faire l’objet
2A-2019-16114-000502

mmigration, Refugees Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

d’une discussion dans le cadre de celle-ci, car il faut du temps pour examiner les éléments de preuve recueillis.

C’est donc à l’API de déterminer la meilleure marche à suivre pour le bon déroulement du cas.

Dans certains cas, par exemple s’il n’y a que quelques feuilles, il pourrait être plus pertinent de demander à ce que les documents soient numérisés, faire une courte pause dans

# l’audience pour les analyser et poursuivre l’audience comme prévue. Cependant, si la

quantité de documents ou la complexité de l’information à analyser est trop importante, il devient illogique de les considérer sur-le-champ. À ce moment-là, l’API déterminera s’il serait préférable de remettre l’audience à plus tard, car les documents à analyser sont importants, ou bien s’il/elle conclut que l’audience sera faite et les documents analysés par la suite.

L’APl peut demander à l’adjoint du bureau local où se trouve le demandeur que les documents apportés le jour de l’audience soient numérisés et lui soient transmis pour être immédiatement consultés. Si l’API l’estime nécessaire (notamment si la preuve est volumineuse ou s’il désire consulter les originaux), le bureau local se chargera de faire parvenir les documents apportés par le demandeur à HM-Vancouver (qui l’enverra au bureau où se trouve l’API).

Si le demandeur se trouve dans un bureau d’IRCC où il n’y a pas de bureau MH, l’API avisera le demandeur de faire parvenir ces documents par courrier ou par courriel aux adresses initialement indiquées dans l’Avis de convocation à une audience d’examen des risques avant renvoi afin qu’ils soient placés au dossier de la demande ERAR. L’API devra alors prendre connaissance de ces documents envoyés par le demandeur à la suite de l’audience.

### Questions Hi IPG,

Centralized Network would like to seek functional guidance, in response to some questions that we’ve received regarding the process of converting an HC application into a Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada Class (SCLPC) application, when the PA has a spousal connection and indicated that they were in agreement with the conversion of their HC application into an SCLPC.

Specifically, can IPG PRPD/IPG APD advise on the following: Once CPC-M is notified by the Domestic Network that a client on an HC application wishes to have their application converted into an SCLPC application, what lock-in date and what received date should be used for the SCLPC application when it is being created? Should the lock in date and received date be the dates the HC application was received in the Domestic Network? Should it be the date where the DN received the client's complete SCLPC forms? Or, Should it be the date that CPC-M receives the documentation of the PA, for their processing of the SCLPC application? Can you also confirm if the received date and the lock-in date would be the same? If not, can you advise which date should be used for the received date and which date should be used for the lock-in date?

- If the client has a spousal connection, agrees to the conversion of their HC application into an SCLPC application, but CPC-M finds that they are not eligible (i.e., the couple is not cohabiting or the PA is subject to a removal order for reasons that are not captured under the spousal public policy), does the application then get transferred back to the Domestic Network, so that it can go back into the HC application stream? Or, does CPC-M refuse the SCLPC application and it is then up to the client to submit another HC application, if they wish to pursue PR status? Based on what the Spousal Public Policy indicates, if the client previously had an HC application, which was then converted into an SCLPC
2A-2019-16114-000513

migration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada ormation disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

application, then they would be transferred back to DN, so that they could be reassessed under the HC stream. However, an HC applicant would not be reassessed under the HC stream, in the event of not being eligible under the SCLPC category if they didn't first have an HC application. Is this correct? Can

## you kindly confirm what the process should be for these types of situations?

## Supervisor / Superviseur : Antoine Bourdeau

## B- To be completed by OMC advisors/à remplir par les conseillers de la DGGOC.

Tracking #/N° de suivi : IM-2014-XXXX Division : APD/DPA Advisor / Conseiller(ère) : Deborah Bodnarok

Answer approved by / Réponse approuvée par : Louise Wanczycki Consulted/Personnes consultées : Answer/Réponse

Thank you for your questions. Please see the responses below.

Question: CN seeks to clarify which lock-in date / received date should be used (and whether these dates are the same or different) as well as what the process should be when the PA (with a former HC application which was converted into an SCLPC application) is deemed to not be eligible under the SCLPC stream. Response:

The lock-in date/received date are the same and should be transferred from the H&C to the newly created SCLPC application (conversion)

The 2005 Public Policy under A25(1) of IRPA to Facilitate Processing in Accordance with the Regulations of the Spouse or Common Law Partner in Canada Class allows for a conversion from an H&C application to an in-Canada spousal application. This policy continues in order to facilitate family reunification and processing in cases where spouses and common-law partners are already living together in Canada.

In such a situation, the officer would propose conversion (if all other requirements appear to be met, most importantly that the spouse qualifies to sponsor), the applicant should be contacted to see if the spouse would be able to make a sponsorship to enable them to benefit from the public policy.

The conversion instructions and background information are detailed in the c Instructions available at:

[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-) agreements/immigration-refugee-protection-act-spousal-policy.html

All case types are listed under Appendix A. Here are the instructions for this particular case type:

### Case 4 New HC1 spousal application

# Action

2A-2019-16114-000514

mmigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Contact client to inform of public policy: if the applicant agrees to have the application assessed under the provisions of the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada class, and submits a sponsorship, applicant is eligible for consideration. If valid sponsorship submitted and the applicant agrees to be assessed under the provisions of the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada class, assess under provisions of this class. If the applicant is found ineligible for the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada class (i.e. invalid sponsorship), refuse the application. Clients are not eligible for the refund provision. If they wish, they may reapply for H&C consideration. Because they agreed to be assessed under the provisions of the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada class, they are not entitled to an H&C reassessment. ●If valid sponsorship not submitted or the applicant does not agree to have the application assessed under the provisions of the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada class, assess under general H&C provisions (separation from a partner not automatic hardship). For those applicants who wished to submit a sponsorship but did not qualify to do so, or who submitted a sponsorship but were found to be ineligible (i.e. invalid sponsorship), this may be considered a positive H&C factor, depending on the reasons for ineligibility. (HC1)

NOTE: The only applications that are returned for a H&C assessment, are transitory cases with a lock-in date prior to February 18, 2005. I note that the department likely has a small number, if any, of these cases.
