Good day Hong Shin, Thank you for contacting IRCC-Immigration Program Guidance Branch. Please find below our response to your query. Question: I am a Border Services Officer working at a Port of Entry in BC. I would like to get some clarification on MI: refusal to process Live-in Caregiver. ([http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/permit-permis/caregiver-aide/refusal-refus-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/permit-permis/caregiver-aide/refusal-refus-eng.aspx)) Does POE application meet the criteria for the refusal to process instructions? Also, it was listed in the program delivery ([http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/port-point-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/work-travail/port-point-) eng.aspx) that people CAN NOT apply for Live-in Caregiver permit upon entry. Would you please provide guidance on processing Live-in Caregivers at POE with LMIA received after 2019-June? For my case scenario, the client entered Canada as a visitor and flag-poled to apply for a work permit. (currently visitor status)

Question: Does POE application meet the criteria for the refusal to process instructions? Response: Yes. If a foreign national has passed Canadian customs, they are considered to have exited the country and should be deemed "outside Canada. Any applications at POE should be considered as such. The language of R198(1) and R190(3)(f) for TRV-required visitors flagpoling would support this interpretation. Application on entry R198 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a foreign national may apply for a work permitwhen entering Canadaif the foreign national is exempt under Division 5 of Part 9 from the requirement to obtain a temporary resident visa. Visa exemption — purpose of entry R190(3) A foreign national is exempt from the requirement to obtain a temporary resident visa if they are seeking to enterand remain in Canada solely

(f)to re-enter Canada following a visit solely to the United States or St. Pierre and Miquelon,
if they

(i) held a study permit or a work permit that was issued before they left Canada on
such a visit or were authorized to enter and remain in Canada as a temporary resident, and (ii) return to Canada by the end of the period initially authorized for their stay or any extension to it; The Ministerial Instructions, issued on June 18, 2019, aim to refuse to process LMIA-work permit applications received from caregivers under the TFWP if the application meets the following criteria:

2A-2019-16114-000517

and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur l’accès à linformation

Officers are instructed not to process applications for new work permits made by foreign nationals under subparagraph 200(1)(c)(iii) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, if all of the below criteria apply

• The intended occupation is in National Occupational Classification (NOC) 4411 (excluding foster parents) or 4412 (excluding housekeepers). The applicant is outside Canada. The applicant is making an initial work permit application (that is, they do not currently hold a valid work permit). The applicant is destined to a job location outside Quebec. The accompanying LMIA application has been received by Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) on or after June 18, 2019.

The applicant is notified of the refusal to process, and the associated work permit processing fee is returned.

It should be noted that the LMIA-required work permit applications submitted by live-in caregivers (Grandfathered program) are not part of the refusal to process. Please refer to Caregiver temporary residence programs comparison table (PDF, 246 KB) for additional information on different options and programs for caregivers. However, Live-in caregivers are not eligible to apply upon entry at the POE.

Question re. Live-in caregivers: All caregivers who are under the grandfathered program (live-in caregiver), are not eligible to apply upon entry under the repealed version of R198(2)(a)(i).

Application on entry

- 198 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a foreign national may apply for a work permit when entering Canada if the foreign national is exempt under Division 5 of Part 9 from the requirement to obtain a temporary resident visa. Exceptions
(2) A foreign national may not apply for a work permit when entering Canada if
(a) a determination under section 203 is required, unless
(i) the Department of Employment and Social Development has provided an assessment under paragraph 203(2)(a) in respect of an offer of employment -other thanseasonal agricultural employmentor employment as a live-in caregiver — to the foreign national,

Good Morning,

It should be noted that cancellation of TRVs is limited to fraud and misrepresentation cases as per the PDIs:

[http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/visa/processing-traitement/cancellation-annulation-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/visa/processing-traitement/cancellation-annulation-eng.aspx)

Please note that IPG is currently reviewing the PDI and will be updating it in the near future.

In this case, as there is no authority to cancel the TRV in the Act or Regs, and subsequently no designated authority to cancel in the Designation of Officers and Delegation of Authority; neither CN nor CBSA should be cancelling these TRVs.

Please be aware that there is progress being made on full cancellation authorities in a new regulatory package, which will be changing these instructions eventually.

## Subject:

### IPG Mailbox, please close this request

Good day Marie-Claude,

#### Thank for your question.

I confirm that the Humanitarian Migration Office in Niagara Falls (HM-NF) processes all of the M5 medical cases for Domestic Network (DN), Centralized Network (CN) and International Network (IN), but only after an officer has determined that the Public Policy (PP) cannot be applied. The current Medical requirements PDI regarding Excessive demand on health services and on social services includes specific IRCC processing network instructions for these cases.

The instructions instructs officers on the steps to complete, depending on either of the following scenarios:

Public policy overcomes excessive demand findings

### Public policy does not overcome excessive demand findings

Once HM-NF receives a M5 case, they are is responsible for sending out the procedural fairness letter (PFL). Permanent Residence (PR) files that are reassessed M3 are processed to completion, NF issues the COPR and queues for granting of PR status. Most Temporary Residence (TR) files that are reassessed M3 are transferred back (electronically) to the home office for finalization.

## Cordially,

Deborah

### IPG Mailbox, please close this request.

## Hi Sophia,

Thanks for reaching out. Following a redetermination decision by the Federal Court (FC), applicants are sent a notice advising that following the FC

## decision, IRCC will study their application for permanent residence from within Canada on humanitarian and

compassionate grounds (H&C). They are provided thirty (30) days to update their application form and written submissions regarding any new element they wish to be considered in the assessment. Below are links to the letters used by the HM-Montreal office. Please ensure to include CMB's office address (header), as well as the decision-maker's title (signature).

QUE-BRA-M-Lettre MAJ CH après un retour de la cour fédérale-Anglais.doc ([http://gcdocs2.ci.gc.ca/otcs/cs.exe/link/29182793](http://gcdocs2.ci.gc.ca/otcs/cs.exe/link/29182793))

QUE-BRA-M-Lettre MAJ CH après un retour de la Cour fédérale-Français.doc ([http://gcdocs2.ci.gc.ca/otcs/cs.exe/link/29182304](http://gcdocs2.ci.gc.ca/otcs/cs.exe/link/29182304))

Note: the same approval/refusal letters are used for all H&C eligibility decisions, including FC redeterminations.

# Thank you,

Deborah Approved by Jacinthe Léveillé Deborah Bodnarok

## Subject:FW: Study Permit Question -- IM-2020-0278 -- DUE March 17, 2020

# Hi Bridget,

Study permit holders on an authorized leave from studies cannot work on campus or off campus, as they are not considered to be full-time students, are not on a regularly scheduled break and, therefore, do not meet the requirements of paragraph R186(f) or (v).

You can find more information in the link below: [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/students-etudiants/assessing-conditions-evaluation-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/students-etudiants/assessing-conditions-evaluation-) eng.aspx#campus

It should be note that a student on leave who begins or resumes their studies within 150 days from the date the leave commenced (that is, the date the leave was granted by the institution) is considered to be actively pursuing studies during their leave. If a student does not resume their studies within 150 days, they should do either of the following:

•change their status (that is, change to visitor status or worker status) •leave Canada

I hope this information has been helpful, if you have further questions please do not hesitate to contact IPG Functional Guidance at IRCC.IPGFunctionalGuidance-OrientationFonctionnelleOPI.IRCC@cic.gc.ca

## Kind regard,

## Subject:RE: Truck driver work permits -- IM-2020-0168

Hi Silvia, Thank you for your email. We understand this issue is appearing with increasing frequency now. While the NOC does specify that certain certifications may be required, in trucking and a number of other professions, foreign nationals will not be able to obtain the necessary Canadian license or certification prior to arrival in Canada. Therefore we cannot expect them to have this in place prior to work permit issuance. Our guidance to migration and border services officers is that they should be satisfied that the applicant can successfully complete the duties of the job (based on prior experience and skillset) and will reasonably be able obtain the necessary requirements to do so in due course. We hope this information is helpful. Sincerely, Tracy Griffiths

Senior Program Advisor, Immigration Program Guidance Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada / Government of Canada Tracy.Griffiths@cic.gc.ca / Tel: 613-297-5355

Conseillere principale de programme, Orientation du programme d’immigration Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada / Gouvernement du Canada Tracy.Griffiths@cic.gc.ca / Tél.: 613-297-5355 From: Graca, Silvia [mailto:Silvia.Graca@cbsa-asfc.gc.ca] Sent: February 10, 2020 9:38 AM To: IPG Functional Guidance / Orientation Fonctionnelle OPI (IRCC); nc-cic exchange-gd@hrsdc-rhdcc.gc.ca Subject: Truck driver work permits Hello IPG, ESDC, Foreign Nationals in the truck driving worker streams are flying to Canada with TRV/WP authorizations approved by visa offices and approved LMlAs with the expectation of receiving a work permit upon arrival at POE, however we have found a complication with the new provincial requirements for truck drivers: applicants are not able to meet the

## Employment requirements

- Completion of secondary school is usually required. · On-the-job-training is provided.
- Completion of an accredited driver training course of up to three duration, through a vocational school or community college, may
- A Class 3 or D licence is required to drive straight-body trucks.
- A Class 1 or A licence is required to drive long combination vehicle
- Air brake endorsement (Z) is required for drivers who operate veh with air brakes.
- Transportation of dangerous goods (TDG) certification is required who transport hazardous products or dangerous goods.
- Additional licensing endorsement or certification may be required articulated trucks.
To mitigate costly inconveniences for the client and industry, we have suggested POEs use the option of issuing visitor permits to allow applicants/employer to obtain the certification (course is under 6 months) and then they have to return to a POE to be issued a WP. But we have also have had situations where clients are having to fly back home to sort out the certification issue and return at a later time. This is not only costly and inconvenient for the client who may have spent much of their savings in travelling to Canada, but it is also not helping an industry already suffering an extreme shortage of drivers. Sharing this with your teams in case there is a way IRCC/ESDC can mitigate these costly and inconvenient occurrences by advising clients/employers to have proof that certification(MELT)is lined up in Canada. Having this proof upon arrival will at least increase the odds of being allowed entry at POEs. Thank you for any feedback and do not hesitate to contact me if you need more information. 1. The Court found there is no requirement for the Applicant to take any steps to prove her intention to live in a province outside Quebec. The Applicant is required only to indicate on the IMMo08 form where they intend to reside. Nowhere does it say that documentation is required to prove this.
2. There is no guidance provided in the Act or the Regulations, nor any policy manuals or bulletins, defining "intend to reside" or setting out what evidence applicants are expected to provide to prove intention. Indeed, until IRCC actually takes issue with an applicant's intentions, a simple confirmation in the immigration application package is sufficient to evidence an intention to settle
3. Given the two points above, the level of PF required in these cases is therefore very high. A request should not be too broad or request that applicant provide evidence of steps taken to reside outside Quebec as this is not a requirement in the Regulations.
4. The Court held that there is no requirement for the Applicant to take up immediate residence in a province outside Quebec (i.e.: assessing the intent within the validity of the visa did not hold-up in Federal Court). We trust that this information will assist you.

Lucinda,

A Visitor Record (VR) does not exist in the Act or Regulations. It is a status document that is issued by either CBSA, to limit or extend a foreign national's stay in Canada, or by IRCC, when a temporary resident has applied for and is approved an extension of their authorized stay in Canada. Once a temporary resident leaves Canada they cease to have temporary resident status, regardless of the expiry date of the VR.

On rare occasions, a Visitor Record is issued with the notation: Departure from Canada does not invalidate this document. The document itself is not invalidated once the foreign national leaves Canada, however, their status as a temporary resident ceases as they are no longer physically present in Canada.

Should a foreign national that was issued a VR with the above notation leave Canada and return, a Border Services Officer may authorize their entry to the validity of the VR or for a different period of time.

R190, as you reference in your enquiry, refers to the exemptions to the TRV requirement. This subsection does not relate to temporary resident status or period of authorized stay.

A Border Services Officer (BSO) has the authority to determine the length of time a temporary resident is authorized to stay in Canada.

time course load in their final academic session -- IM-2020-0091 -- DUE 7-Feb-20

Good day Valerie,

This is in response to your question regarding work on-campus with part-time course load.

As per R186(f), only full-time students may engage in employment on campus of the university or college at which they are a full-time student. Students who have maintained full-time status for the duration of their program of study, and who only require a part-time course load in their final academic session in order to complete their program of study, may only work off campus up to 20 hours per week during their final academic session.

I hope that this information is helpful to you. If you have any further questions, please contact :

Thank you for your question. The phrase you highlighted below refers to criminal proceedings and has no link to your involvement on the administrative side. This section is included in the PDl as background information about how the criminal justice system works (or can work) when making the equivalency determination. It does not represent instructions for IRCC or CBSA decision-makers when dealing with young offenders. As such, you are not required to petition the criminal court for anything with regards to young offender sentencing and can proceed as per the instructions in the PDI.

## Subject: Youth Convictions received Abroad-IRCC Policy requiring clarification

### Good morning,

We have received queries from our Hearings Officers with regards to the application of the IRCC policy on youth convictions abroad.

In IRPA, the exception to 36(1)(a) is 36(3)(e)(ii) and (ii), wherein it is explicit that those subsections are only applicable to those convicted/sentenced under the YOA or YCJA, thereby inferring that such an exception does not extend to foreign offences captured under 36(1)(b) or (c). However a recent IRCC policy on the matter introduces a new concept

## of “equivalency” or youth convictions abroad.

Here is an excerpt from the relevant section [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/standard/rehab-readapt/factors-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/standard/rehab-readapt/factors-) facteurs-eng.aspx:

What to consider in determining whether an adult sentence would have been imposed in Canada Young persons who have been arrested and charged with an offence in Canada may, in certain circumstances, be at risk of receiving an adult sentence if they are found guilty. For this situation to arise, the offence must have been both:

one that would attract a penalty of more than two years if committed by an adult alleged to have been committed when the young person was fourteen years of age or older

If a young person is 14 years of age or older and is charged with a serious violent offence,the prosecutor must considerapplying to the court for an adult sentence.The courtcan impose an adult sentence only if both:

- the presumption that the young person has diminished moral blameworthiness or culpability is rebutted
2A-2019-16114-000563

- a youth sentence would not be of sufficient length to hold the young person accountable
It is unclear how [CBSA or IRCC] officers can "apply to the Court" in our administrative law setting to determine if the "Court" would grant such an application.

# Could you please provide operational guidance on the application of this policy position?
